stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Legora announced Intake on 13 October, a front door for in-house legal teams built around the Legora Agent. Intake turns legal requests into tracked work and is available now in Slack, according to the source.

stories.t: Italian Court Orders Google to Overhaul Right-to-Be-Forgotten Process in Latest European Setback
stories.s: An Italian court has ordered Google to overhaul its right-to-be-forgotten process, according to Legal Tech Monitor, which reported the ruling on 13 October. The article describes it as the latest setback for Google in Europe, following legal action and multimillion-dollar fines.

stories.t: On the Road in Atlanta: Messy Data, Runaway Pilots, and Lessons from the GDS AI Summit
stories.s: Greg Lambert and Marlene Gebauer record a podcast from Atlanta after the GDS AI Summit, discussing messy data, unclear data ownership and pressures on legal technology. It is commentary rather than news.

stories.s: Legal Business gathers reactions from national law firm leaders to Andy Burnham's devolution drive, including a quote from Sarah Walton, managing partner at Weightmans, who says the Manchester buzz around Number 10 North will fade and outcomes will matter. The piece focuses on the political agenda for the North of England.

stories.t: Judiciary gives AI cautious thumbs-up (but draws line at robot judges)
stories.s: The judiciary has given a cautious endorsement to the use of AI, promoting strict safeguards and robust testing, but has drawn a line at robot judges, according to Legal Cheek. The extract is brief and does not name the judicial body or the guidance.

stories.t: SRA names new chair - with pledge to lead change
stories.s: Caroline Corby is to become chair of the Solicitors Regulation Authority, replacing Anna Bradley, according to The Law Society Gazette. Corby joins from a healthcare regulator. The report says she has pledged to lead change.

stories.t: 'Dark day for international justice': legal chiefs condemn US sanctions on ICC
stories.s: The Law Society and the International Bar Association condemned US sanctions on the International Criminal Court, saying perpetrators of serious crimes may escape punishment. A landmark report also found weaknesses in the UK approach to atrocity crimes.

stories.t: High Court chastises MoD over repeated deadline failures
Law Society highlights plight of 'vital' small firms
stories.s: The Law Society says small firms are vital and that their sustainability is likely to be a key focus at the Society's AGM. The item is a brief preview from the Law Society Gazette.

stories.t: Barrister who was part of £1.8m legal aid scam disbarred
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that a barrister involved in a £1.8m legal aid fraud has been disbarred. The practitioner was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court in June 2024 to three years' imprisonment. The report concerns professional regulation and sanctions for a member of the bar convicted over the scheme.

stories.t: ‘Bankruptcy Tourism’ Ruling Prompts New Ch. 15 Challenges
stories.s: Troutman Pepper Locke partner Evelyn J. Meltzer was quoted on 13 October 2026 on a bankruptcy tourism ruling and new Chapter 15 challenges. The firm published the commentary on its own site.

stories.t: From AI Tools to Agentic AI – A Roadmap
stories.s: Paul Walker, Global Solutions Director at iManage, has written an Artificial Lawyer opinion piece setting out a roadmap from AI tools to agentic AI. He argues that law firms have long delegated work to less experienced staff. The extract is an opinion piece by a vendor executive.

stories.s: Legal Futures reports that drivers are considering litigation rather than waiting for the legal challenge to the FCA motor finance compensation scheme. The challenge's hearing has now been set for February. The extract is brief and does not give the hearing's court or further detail.

stories.s: Mitratech promotes an on-demand webinar on how enterprise legal teams build defensible legal hold programmes. The post is a vendor event notice with no further detail in the extract.

stories.s: The CCBE, the body representing Europe's bar associations, has published an item on its participation at the International Bar Association's Annual Conference. stories.s: Morrison & Foerster reports that California's SB 574 is the first state law to regulate attorneys' use of generative AI. The firm says the new disclosure, verification and confidentiality rules should be learned before 1 January 2027. The post is dated 14 October 2026.

stories.s: Legora, an AI vendor for legal teams, promotes its tools for in-house lawyers, covering first-pass review, drafting and research. The page says the product helps lean in-house teams keep more work in-house. No figures or dates are given.

stories.s: Summize is promoting an on-demand webinar on the AI Fluency Report, which it says covers legal AI adoption, governance and verification. The session is aimed at in-house teams. No date or figures are given in the extract.

The article argues that trial court records can show judges' performance and decision-making. It is dated 14 October 2026.

stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports that some legal technology companies may move from seat-based to consumption-based pricing, and that law firms are considering how to keep AI costs down. The brief extract gives no figures or named firms. It is dated 14 October 2026.

stories.t: AI Could Kill the Junior Lawyer Pipeline; Is Banning it the Answer?
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor asks whether banning AI use is the right response to fears that it will erode the junior lawyer pipeline. The piece notes that AI now leads on research, drafting and document review, and that firms are struggling to keep junior lawyers building skills through repetitive work. It is dated 14 October 2026.

stories.t: ILTA Releases 2026 Compensation Survey Results Report, Delivering Critical Legal Technology Salary and Workforce Insights
stories.s: ILTA has released its 2026 Compensation Survey Results Report, which provides benchmarking data and trend analysis on legal technology salaries and workforce planning. The release is dated October 2026 and was announced by ILTA, according to the aggregator copy.

stories.s: The Lady Chief Justice attended the unveiling of a blue plaque honouring Gertrude Tuckwell, a pioneering female magistrate. The judiciary publication says the plaque recognises her lasting impact on the justice system. No date for the ceremony is given in the extract.

stories.s: Sir Geoffrey Vos, Master of the Rolls, gave the main keynote at the Legal Geek Conference. According to the judiciary's published speech, he addressed how technology will change the delivery of legal services and dispute resolution. The extract does not give the date of the speech.

stories.s: The judiciary has advertised a vacancy for a Deputy District Judge with applications closing on Tuesday 27 October 2026. The notice is published on the Courts and Tribunals Judiciary site. The extract does not give the location or terms of the role.

stories.s: Legal Business reports that Manchester-based Centrefield has taken private equity investment from Palatine, which will invest £254m. stories.s: The Law Society says small law firms are being deterred from taking on solicitor apprentices because of changes to apprenticeship funding. stories.t: Legal Innovators UK Starts Tomorrow – Nov 4th
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer announces that the Legal Innovators UK event starts on Wednesday 4 November and runs through Thursday 5 November. The article is a short event notice. It gives no programme details in the extract.

stories.s: Hg, the private equity firm that owns Litera, and AI company Anthropic have invested in an 'AI Transformation' venture, along with some angel investors. stories.s: Co-Flo has launched AI-powered matter management functionality that combines financial data from practice management systems with real-time matter progress inside iManage. The product is aimed at law firms. The announcement is reported by Legal IT Insider.

stories.t: AI law firms circle Weil’s assets and lawyers as it winds down
stories.s: Nonbillable reports that AI-focused law firms Vetta, Scissero and Crosby are interested in the technology, IP and lawyers of Weil, Gotshal and Manges, the US firm that is winding down after a dramatic collapse. The report does not give terms of any deal.

stories.t: 'Strong and stable': Weil’s UK profits soared before firm’s shock demise
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that Weil's UK arm reported rising profits in the first half of 2026, with bosses citing sustained demand and a strong liquidity position. The report comes before the firm's sudden collapse.

stories.t: FCA fires claims warning as Barclays goes early on motor finance redress
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that the FCA has warned customers they do not need a law firm or claims management company to claim on motor finance redress, as Barclays moves early on redress. The article says the matter is at a legal deadlock.

stories.t: Support staff face axe as £27m merger deal completes
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that support staff face redundancy as the £27m merger of Knights and Moore Barlow completes. According to the extract, Moore Barlow joins the Knights business and strengthens the national firm's presence in the south east. The story concerns law firm consolidation and its effect on staffing.

stories.t: Ombudsman braced for 21,000 lawyer complaints next year
stories.s: The Legal Ombudsman expects around 21,000 complaints about lawyers next year, according to the Law Society Gazette. It says the rise in reports outpaces the growth in resolved cases.

stories.s: The Commons Justice Committee has criticised the government's response to legal aid, saying its monitoring of declining provision with promised later solutions is inadequate. The Law Society Gazette reports the committee's position.

Lawyers in Canada face deepfake risks, and Ontario's proposed AI evidence rules would presume some undisclosed AI-generated evidence inadmissible. The Civil Rules Review Working Group's December 2025 report proposes a reliance-based disclosure model. Several lawyers are quoted, including Emily Hazlett, Kelly Friedman and Kathryn Manning.

The guidance says legal representatives must book with approved providers unless HMCTS agrees otherwise.

stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Jus Mundi has added an AI-powered arbitrator search to its Jus AI product. According to the item, the feature helps arbitration lawyers identify potential arbitrators and research shortlisted candidates. The extract is brief and does not describe pricing or availability.

stories.t: New York State Bar Association tells lawyers not to bill for time saved by AI
stories.s: The New York State Bar Association's Committee on Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technologies has issued a report, adopted by the governing body, on billing for AI. Per Law360, the report treats AI software costs as overhead that can be passed on as a disbursement only when tied to a specific client matter and disclosed. Lawyers need not tell clients about AI use for purely administrative tasks, provided fees are unaffected. NYSBA president Taa Grays says the guidance is meant to help attorneys use AI ethically.

He describes the legal context graph, launched earlier this year, which maps relationships among matters, documents and people. Hauck also covers general availability of tabular review, document generation and redlining, and a beta MCP connector with Legora.

The item concerns the document management vendor NetDocuments and its conference announcements.

stories.t: Connecticut’s AI Rules Take Shape: What Employers and Developers Need to Know // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley analyses Connecticut's SB 5, signed on 27 May 2026 as Public Act 26-15, focusing on employment-related AI rules. Employer disclosure and notice duties start on 1 October 2027, and the attorney general enforces them with no private right of action. The alert flags that the 'materially influence' test may be broader than New York City's law.

stories.t: Risk Management Tips For Cos. Deploying Open-Weight AI // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley partners William K. Pao, Tracy Rubin, Sean Quinn and Brian Nelson have written an article for Law360 on the legal and operational risks of deploying open-weight AI models. It covers licensing, intellectual property, privacy and cybersecurity, and includes a pre-deployment checklist. The item is a relayed law firm thought piece.

stories.t: FCA Enforcement Monthly | Morrison Foerster
stories.s: Morrison Foerster's monthly False Claims Act newsletter covers Medicare Advantage chart-review settlements, including Independence Blue Cross paying $22.5m, and DOJ's opioid pharmacy cases, including CVS paying $315m.

stories.t: UK judge elected to international court
stories.s: Professor Dapo Akande, a fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, has been elected a judge of the International Court of Justice after a vote by UN Member States, according to Solicitors Journal. The article says he will serve a nine-year term and that the election marks the return of a UK judge to the court after almost a decade. It quotes the Prime Minister and the Foreign Secretary welcoming the result.

stories.t: Is it time to reform legal services regulation?
stories.s: Solicitors Journal publishes a commentary arguing that gaps in the statutory framework for legal services regulation are now exposed. It cites the High Court ruling in Carter-Ruck that the SRA cannot compel privileged material without client consent, now subject to a leapfrog appeal to the Supreme Court, and the Court of Appeal's Mazur decision on conduct of litigation. The author, who acted for the Law Society in Mazur, calls for reform.

The extract is mainly site navigation and does not set out the deal price or integration timeline. The release is dated 3 November 2026 in the catalogue.

stories.t: Turning a Loose Field Definition Into a Reliable Contract Extraction
stories.s: Docusign has published part three of a series on how it processes contracts at scale, explaining how custom extractions reach the accuracy of its standard models without training a new model for each field.

stories.t: Preservation, Proportionality, Privilege, and Prompts: The 13th Annual Judicial Panel | Relativity Blog | Relativity
stories.s: Relativity's blog reports on its 13th Annual Judicial Panel at RelFest, with five judges from federal, state and England and Wales courts. The panel discussed AI hallucinations, citing Damien Charlotin's tracker, which the blog says has risen from over 400 cases in October 2025 to 2,262. Judges offered views on candour, the scale of the problem and AI use.

Summize Sign | Electronic Signature Software
stories.s: Summize has promoted Summize Sign, a native eSignature feature inside its contract lifecycle management platform, which it says removes the need for a separate signing tool.

stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports that at least two AI-native law firms have bid for data belonging to Weil, Gotshal & Manges. The piece raises whether internal law firm data counts as an asset that an outside buyer can acquire. The extract is brief and does not name the bidders.

stories.t: Illinois Supreme Court Amends Rule 10-101 Standardized Court Forms, Addressing Unauthorized Practice of Law Concerns
stories.s: The Illinois Supreme Court amended Rule 10-101 on standardised court forms, effective 15 October 2026, clarifying that providing forms is not unauthorised practice of law.

stories.t: Close Calls: An Interactive Look at the Redgrave Study: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.s: Doug Austin on eDiscovery Today describes a Relativity interactive game built on the Redgrave study of aiR Review. Players classify ten close-call documents from a 45,004-document Mallinckrodt set and compare their calls with four teams. The author reports he matched the aiR team on eight of ten documents and notes only two documents drew unanimous classification.

stories.t: The Jumpstart Outline from The Sedona Conference: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.s: Doug Austin reports that The Sedona Conference's Working Group 1 has published a new draft of the Jumpstart Outline for member and public comment. The 32-page update covers AI, generative AI and newer data sources. Comments are open until 11 December 2026, and the final version is due in January 2027.

stories.t: 9 Tips and Questions to Ask When Choosing an eDiscovery Vendor: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.s: Doug Austin on eDiscovery Today republishes a sponsored guest post from Nextpoint on choosing an eDiscovery vendor. The post cites ILTA's 2026 Technology Survey, which reports 94 per cent of firms using or exploring generative AI, and 8am's finding that most firms lack formal AI policies. Nextpoint is disclosed as an Educational Partner and sponsor of the blog.

stories.t: The practical guide to Data Subject Access Requests
stories.s: Mishcon de Reya has published a practical guide to data subject access requests (DSARs). The firm describes DSARs as a significant compliance and operational challenge for organisations. The extract is a short summary, so the guide's detailed steps and recommendations are not covered here.

He also notes a rise in AI-native law firms, and promotes the Legal Innovators UK and New York conferences.

Scissero has expressed interest in Weil's technology, IP and data, Crosby has bid for its trademark and data, and Vetta wants precedents and lawyers. The piece cites an $85m raise at Crosby and a $10m bid for airline data as a benchmark, and says no asset transfer has been announced.

Partners are reported to be leaving across the market.

stories.s: Legal Cheek reports that complaints to the Bar Standards Board about barristers' social media posts more than doubled, from 132 to 279, in 2025-26, according to the regulator's annual report. Most related to the Israel-Palestine conflict. The BSB also concluded 114 investigations, with 51 per cent referred for disciplinary action. Phil Golding, the BSB's director general, cited operational pressure.

stories.t: Is Google becoming pay-to-play for law firms?
stories.s: Legal Futures publishes a sponsored commentary by Stacey Horrocks of BSD Legal Marketing on how Google search has changed for law firms. It notes expanded paid placement, the April 2025 auction change and the October 2025 'Sponsored results' grouping. The author argues rankings no longer equal visibility and that firms should track enquiries from search.

stories.t: SRA “keeping close eye” on accumulator law firms

stories.s: Legal Futures reports that Manifest OS, a US AI-native immigration business, has made its first UK hire, Sophy King, as president of international immigration. The company plans to expand to more than 100 jurisdictions and open 40 offices within a year, starting with a London office. The UK operation would be regulated by the Immigration Advice Authority, according to King.

stories.t: Trainee solicitor and paralegal banned for sexual offences convictions
stories.s: Legal Futures reports that the SRA has made section 43 orders barring a trainee solicitor at Southampton University's legal services department and a former Ramsdens paralegal from working in SRA-regulated practice without approval. Both were convicted of sexual offences involving children, and the SRA says the convictions make their involvement in legal practice undesirable.

stories.t: Dismay over government response to MPs’ legal aid report
stories.s: Four legal advice charities have expressed dismay after the government did not accept any of the 28 recommendations in the justice select committee's report on legal aid. The committee said it interpreted the government as having rejected or declined to comment on all of them. The Ministry of Justice called the system inherited in crisis and cited extra funding figures.

stories.t: Moore Barlow sale to Fletchers driven by “need to invest in technology”
stories.s: Legal IT Insider reports that the sale of Moore Barlow to Fletchers was driven by a need to invest in technology. The extract is a site verification page only, so the buyer's reasoning and the deal terms are not set out here. It is a companion story to coverage of Knights' acquisition of part of the same firm.

stories.t: Widespread redundancies follow Knights’ acquisition of 70% of Moore Barlow’s business
stories.s: Legal IT Insider reports that widespread redundancies have followed Knights' acquisition of around 70 per cent of the business of Moore Barlow. The extract is a site verification page only, so the scale of job losses and the deal terms are not confirmed here. The piece is a sister story to coverage of the Fletchers sale of Moore Barlow, and the two should be read together for the transaction details.

stories.t: Simmons and HSF Kramer advise on London’s largest mining IPO since 2018
'Retraumatised': Grieving father received court bundle evening before inquest
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that Johnny Santer, an unrepresented father, received a disclosure bundle at 7.30pm the evening before his son's inquest, told the House of Commons justice select committee. INQUEST's Deborah Coles said the government has yet to decide the trigger point for legal aid for inquests under Hillsborough law.
e: House of Commons justice select committee

stories.t: Solicitors invited to contribute to review of police accountability
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that solicitors and others are invited to submit evidence to the review of police accountability, which runs to 15 January 2027. IOPC figures show more than 108,000 police complaints in 2025/26, up 15 per cent, though the IOPC says recording changes contributed. Co-chairs Dame Lynne Owens and Jason Beer KC are quoted.

stories.t: CPS cited non-existent authority in rape prosecution
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports a High Court judgment in LYC v DPP in which the CPS cited a non-existent authority, R v J [2024] EWCA Crim 3529, in a written record for a prosecution. The court found the citation unsatisfactory but held it did not affect the outcome, refused permission to amend and dismissed the judicial review. The claimant was 14 and the alleged offence occurred when he was 11.

stories.t: Personal injury heavyweights swallow up more of the claims sector
stories.s: Express Solicitors has bought Ralli Ltd, a Sale-based personal injury firm with around 40 staff, according to The Law Society Gazette. Ralli's accounts for the year to June 2025 show pre-tax profit of £391,000 on revenue of about £3.8m. Express says it now has more than 1,000 staff and turnover of £65m for the year to August 2025.

stories.t: Legal academic elected as first UK International Court of Justice judge in a decade
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that Professor Dapo Akande has been elected to the International Court of Justice, the first British judge in a decade. He will serve nine years. The UK prime minister and foreign secretary welcomed the result, and the election also filled seats for France, Jordan, Singapore and Kenya.

stories.t: Weil trainees rescued as Gibson Dunn prepares to hire dozens of lawyers
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that Latham & Watkins has hired five trainees from the collapsing Weil, Gotshal & Manges London office, and that Gibson Dunn is expected to complete the hire of around 120 Weil private funds lawyers, including over 20 partners. Weil's leaders have recommended an orderly wind-down, according to the Gazette.

stories.t: His Master's voice: Sir Geoffrey Vos's greatest hits
stories.s: Outgoing Master of the Rolls Sir Geoffrey Vos's six years in office are reviewed against his technology predictions, from 2018 forecasts on digital evidence to his views on AI in judicial decision-making.

stories.t: Use of QES at Land Registry has “rocketed” in latest quarter, new data suggests
Your First Home price caps revealed ranging from £215,000 to £650,000.
LeO to consult on new strategy as demand for its service outpaces capacity
Half of local planning authorities fail to discharge planning conditions within timeframe, analysis found
Profile: Catherine Shiers, customer engagement director at Groundsure
How Norrie Waite & Slater mitigate modern probate risk with Estatesearch
stories.s: Today's Wills and Probate has published a firm profile on Norrie Waite & Slater and its use of Estatesearch to manage modern probate risk. The extract, however, carries a headline about a Law Society response to the Civil Justice Council's AI report, so the text supplied does not match the title. Details of the firm's approach are not visible in the extract.

stories.t: Law Society welcomes CJC’s AI report but warns of potential for ‘misleading documents’
stories.s: Today's Wills and Probate reports that the Law Society has welcomed the Civil Justice Council's report on AI but warns of the potential for misleading documents. The extract shows only a sidebar item about a judicial appointment, so the report's recommendations are not set out here.

stories.t: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith appointed Deputy President of the Business and Property Division
Independent study on the impact of age assurance on fundamental rights and costs for businesses
stories.s: The European Commission publishes an independent study on age assurance, covering its effects on fundamental rights and costs for businesses, including small firms. The study was carried out by an external contractor and was commissioned to inform the proposed EU KIDS Act. It finds costs are likely to remain modest, and it highlights the EU age verification blueprint as a potentially affordable route for providers.

stories.t: Call for evidence on advertising repositories
stories.s: The European Commission is seeking feedback through a call for evidence on forthcoming guidelines for advertising repositories under the Digital Services Act. The guidelines will cover searchability, targeting insights and accessibility of ads on very large platforms and search engines. A targeted public consultation follows in 2027, with publication planned for the second quarter of 2028.

stories.t: Police accountability
stories.s: The Home Office secretariat is seeking views and evidence for the independent end-to-end review of the police accountability system. The review is chaired by Dame Lynne Owens and Jason Beer KC. The call for evidence closes at 11.59pm on 15 January 2027 and is separate from a Ministry of Justice consultation on the standard of proof for unlawful killing conclusions.

stories.t: Lawfront appoints new Group CMO Owen
Browne Jacobson advises on care home sale
Professionalism Spotlight: Melissa Kallio, Dutton Casey & Mesoloras, P.C.
Massachusetts Judge Throws Out DOJ Bid for Harvard Admissions Data
stories.s: A federal judge in Massachusetts has dismissed the US Department of Justice's lawsuit seeking to make Harvard University produce applicant-level admissions records. The DOJ sought the data in an investigation into whether Harvard kept using race-conscious admissions after the 2023 Students for Fair Admissions decision. The dismissal leaves the underlying allegations unresolved. Legal Tech Monitor frames the ruling as a procedural win relevant to discovery and data governance.

stories.t: What listening taught me about leading growth in the AI era
Lawyers’ AI use doesn’t justify slashing $115K fee award, appellate court says
stories.s: According to Reuters, the US 10th Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a $115,000 fee award to Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck, defence counsel in a trade secrets dispute brought by Flux Drive. The panel said plaintiffs had not shown that the use of AI made the hours actually worked unreasonable. The court also upheld dismissal of the lawsuit. Judge Carolyn McHugh wrote the unanimous opinion, stressing that lawyers must still verify authorities themselves.

stories.t: Judiciary efforts to create rules for AI stalling amid concerns
stories.s: The ABA Journal, citing a Law360 story, reports that efforts to write rules on artificial intelligence use in US federal courts have stalled. The Advisory Committee on Evidence Rules, which advises the Judicial Conference, has faced setbacks and resistance, including criticism of a proposed rule on AI deepfakes. Maura R. Grossman, a University of Waterloo professor whose research shaped the proposals, told Law360 she was not hopeful.
e: Judicial Conference of the United States

stories.t: Biglaw Firms That Surrendered To Trump Should Get Ready For The Congressional Probes
Gibson Dunn Could Roll Out The Welcome Mat For Up To 120 Weil Lawyers
stories.s: Above the Law, citing the Financial Times, reports that Gibson Dunn is in talks to hire as many as 120 Weil lawyers across the US and London, including more than 20 partners. The group includes Andrew Chizzik, head of Weil's New York private funds practice, and James Bromley and James Sargent, London co-heads. Weil is preparing to wind down after partner departures and failed merger talks. Neither firm commented.

stories.t: Former Weil Partners Lawyer Up As The Firm’s Wind-Down Turns Into A Fight Over What’s Left
stories.s: Above the Law, citing the Financial Times, reports that a group of about 10 former Weil Gotshal partners has hired Peter Wang, a Foley & Lardner litigator, over the firm's wind-down. The group is said to be probing whether there was a breach of fiduciary duty by Weil's leadership. Separately, Ramona Nee is reported to be moving to Kirkland & Ellis with a team, with Bloomberg Law and Law.com giving differing headcounts.

stories.t: The FTC Is Flexing Its Muscle In Healthcare
Chiropractic lawsuits: two routes to a claim
Slaughters leads for Anthropic on UK share offer in IPO
Gibson Dunn expands Weil funds raid to US in 120-lawyer swoop
Intellectual Property Office gets new weapons to protect design
stories.s: The government has announced changes to UK design law, after a 2025 IPO consultation found that resolving design disputes falls heavily on small firms, some spending £10,000 to £50,000. Proposals include IPO powers to check novelty and refuse bad-faith applications, a route for registered design cases in the IPEC Small Claims Track, a 30-month deferment period and wider unregistered design protection. Legislation will follow when parliamentary time allows.

stories.t: 'Sycophantic' AI inflaming litigants in person, digital justice expert claims
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that Dr Natalie Byrom, in a report for the Nuffield Family Justice Observatory, warns that sycophantic AI advice tools are misleading litigants in person in family courts. She urges the MoJ and HMCTS to assess vendor lock-in and sovereignty risks, reduce reliance on a small number of foreign AI developers, and consider registration rather than reserved activity for AI advice tools. The report criticises a delegation-by-default approach.

stories.t: InTouch partners with The Search Bureau
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer reports that use of qualified electronic signatures (QES) at the Land Registry has risen sharply in the latest quarter, according to new data. The extract is only the article's opening line and does not name the figures. The item is headlined as a partnership between InTouch and The Search Bureau, so the headline and the extract appear to describe different stories. Readers should treat the piece as relating to conveyancing and e-signature use.

stories.t: BigLaw partners with Big Tech to design and deploy custom AI tools
Trial opens for suspect whose multiple email threats include ‘skinning’ federal judge
stories.s: Opening statements were made in the trial of David Brooks Pokorny, 45, of El Cerrito, California, who is charged with making felony threats against a judicial officer. Prosecutor Kent Stejskal told the jury that 11 emails sent in 44 minutes to assault, kidnap and murder Judge Charles Breyer were true threats. The defence argues the emails are protected free speech. Judge Jon Tigar is presiding.

stories.t: AI Connectors For E-Discovery: Great To Drive, But There Are Speed Limits
stories.s: A columnist for Above the Law warns that Reveal's Onna platform can now collect conversations employees generate in Claude Enterprise, following earlier support for ChatGPT and Gemini. The column argues that prompts and AI outputs may be discoverable and urges in-house teams to train staff on the risk. It is commentary on e-discovery tooling and employee AI use.

stories.t: AI May Speed Up Legal Research, But That Doesn’t Automatically Shrink The Bill
stories.s: The Tenth Circuit panel, in an opinion by Judge Carolyn McHugh, affirmed a $114,663.11 fee award to Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck after Flux Drive's trade secrets suit was dismissed. Flux Drive had argued the firm's use of AI and online research tools should have cut its fees, but the court said it pointed to no specific inflated billing entry. The panel noted AI may reduce research time while lawyers must still verify their authorities.

stories.t: Trump-Pardoned J6er Who Threatened To Shoot Pelosi Now Charged With Threatening To Execute Judges
There’s one week left to register for the Lexpert Rising Stars Awards
AI Firm Bids For Weil Assets Spotlight Firm Data Value
Luminance Promotes Counsel To Data Protection Officer Role
stories.s: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech reports that Luminance has promoted a member of its counsel team to the role of data protection officer. The outlet summary gives no further detail on the individual or the scope of the role. The item is a short personnel update about a legal AI vendor.

stories.t: Pierson Ferdinand Adds Partners From Constangy, Akerman
Kiwi Legal AI Company Ivo Scores Major US Sports Deal With NBA and NHL Teams
stories.s: Ivo, a legal AI company founded in New Zealand and now based in San Francisco, has signed a multi-year partnership with Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment. The deal names Ivo the exclusive legal AI partner of the Philadelphia 76ers, New Jersey Devils and Prudential Center, and HBSE's in-house team will use Ivo for contract drafting, negotiation and research. The item relies largely on Ivo's own announcement, which quotes co-founder and CEO Min-Kyu Jung.

stories.t: Dentons Reshuffles Global Leadership As BigLaw Focuses On Cross-Border Efficiency
Latest US Map of Copyright Suits v. AI. Total = 161
stories.s: Edward Lee's blog updates its US map of copyright suits against AI companies to a total of 161, adding three cases: Boone Newsmedia v Microsoft, and two suits against Brave Software by The New York Times and Daily News.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Harvey and Jus Mundi partner to bring Jus AI into Harvey - LegalTechTalk
Newcode and iManage team up on AI access to governed firm content - LegalTechTalk
stories.s: LegalTechTalk reports that Newcode has formed a technology alliance with iManage, linking Newcode's Nova AI workspace to iManage content while keeping existing permissions and security in place. The extract is a short summary, so the terms of the alliance and launch timing cannot be confirmed from it.

stories.t: When AI Becomes the Activist’s Thesis | Insights & Resources | Goodwin
stories.s: Goodwin says AI-themed shareholder activism in the 2026 proxy season shifted from governance to valuation, citing Findell Capital's Figma campaign and Engine Capital's approach to EPAM Systems. Barclays data is cited for H1 2026 campaigns.

stories.t: MoFo Advises Docusign on Acquisition of Suplari | Morrison Foerster
stories.s: Morrison Foerster advised Docusign on its acquisition of Suplari, an AI-native procurement intelligence company. Docusign says the deal will bring Suplari's technology into its Intelligent Agreement Management platform and speed up its procurement tools. The MoFo team was led by corporate partner Jackie Liu and included partners across compensation, employment, technology transactions and privacy.

stories.t: Blandy & Blandy now welcomes training contract applications
Fox Williams expands technology team with partner
R v Bush: charging and sentencing without a clear framework
Stronger design protection for UK creators
Local voices will guide water management
A&O Shearman invests heavily in AI strategy
Docusign Named a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Contract Life-Cycle Management Software for Corporate Legal
stories.s: Docusign says it has been named a leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for worldwide contract lifecycle management software for corporate legal. The page also refers to a 2026 Inc. Power Partner Award. The extract is limited to headings, so the evaluation criteria and the wider report cannot be confirmed from it.

stories.t: Facts & Chronologies | Harvey
stories.s: Harvey's product page describes a facts and chronologies feature that turns large document sets into structured facts, timelines and draft work product with links back to sources. The page is vendor marketing and makes no independent claims.

stories.t: How to Manage Compliance Requests Without Losing Control
stories.s: Neota Logic publishes a guide on managing compliance requests through a single intake channel, with rule-based classification, named owners and full audit trails. The piece argues that AI should be used for drafting, classification and summarising, with a human checkpoint where risk is material. It sets out which requests count as compliance requests, including regulator follow-ups, vendor sign-offs and third-party subpoenas, and closes with a section on how Neota Logic supports the process.

stories.t: Clio Says AI Is Boosting Billable Hours: Maybe I Was Wrong. Or Maybe Not
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor, relaying Above the Law, says Clio's report found billable hours are rising as AI adoption grows, which the writer had not expected. The writer spoke with Clio's Lenon at the conference and suggests the trend may not be long-term. The piece is commentary on Clio's 2026 Legal Trends Report, with the data detailed in a companion story.

stories.t: Lawyers Are Billing More Time as AI Adoption Grows, According to 2026 Clio Legal Trends Report
stories.s: Clio's 2026 Legal Trends Report says 85 per cent of surveyed legal professionals report some AI adoption at their firms, and that billable utilisation is projected to rise 3.1 percentage points in 2026. Clio says the figure is the largest one-year increase in the report's history. The survey also found 64 per cent of AI-using respondents say it is positively affecting revenue, up from 36 per cent in 2025.

stories.t: AI Could Give the Billable Hour New Life. Here's Why Legal Departments May Welcome It
Generative Legal's Cornell Tech Conference: ‘Productizing' Legal Work in the AI Age
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports on a Generative Legal conference at Cornell Tech in which panellists discussed how AI is reshaping legal business models. Topics included law firms embedding their expertise in software and in-house teams facing decision paralysis in a crowded technology market. The extract is a short standfirst, so speakers and specific remarks cannot be confirmed.

stories.t: New PTAB Challenge Filed in IPR2027-00029 Involving Shining 3D Tech
Google Scores Partial Victory as EU Adviser Shifts Copyright Focus to Chatbots
Insight Optix Introduces Enterprise-Wide Legal Hold Intelligence with Latest Release of Legal Hold Evolve™
stories.s: Insight Optix has released a major update to Legal Hold Evolve, adding enterprise-wide legal hold intelligence, automated workflows and new data integrations including Google Workspace, Box and Dropbox. Chief executive Mandi Ross says knowledge from each matter can become a lasting enterprise asset. The release was announced on 4 November 2026 according to the press release reproduced in the blog post.

stories.t: Community Spotlight: Lord John Thomas
stories.s: Legal Geek interviews Lord John Thomas, former Lord Chief Justice, on implementing AI in courts and arbitration. He describes his work on court IT, including the government's large court IT investment when he was Lord Chief Justice, and his chairing of the Standing International Forum of Commercial Courts' steering committee, whose current project is AI. He advises legal tech founders to build tools that draw only on reliable legal sources and give accurate, checkable references.
e: Standing International Forum of Commercial Courts

stories.t: If You Want Business Contacts To Remember You, Consider Giving Gifts In November
Westlaw AI Fight Warrants Full Court Review, 3rd Circ. Told
stories.s: Law360 Pulse reports that a Westlaw AI dispute warrants full court review, according to a filing or argument before the Third Circuit. The extract is only a headline-level summary, so the parties, the procedural posture and the reasons for the request cannot be confirmed from the text. The dispute concerns Thomson Reuters' Westlaw AI product.

stories.t: NZ Law – Family violence system failing survivors, report finds
What Is the Difference Between State and Federal Criminal Charges in Florida?
How Do Alabama Right-of-Way Laws Affect Car Accident Claims?
Weil’s Former Partners Hire Counsel as the Wind-Down Turns to Who Gets Paid
stories.s: LawFuel reports, citing the Financial Times and Reuters, that about ten former Weil Gotshal partners have hired Foley & Lardner litigator Peter Wang as the firm heads for closure. The firm reportedly wants an out-of-court dissolution, with AlixPartners and Davis Polk advising. The FT reports former partners are examining whether management breached fiduciary duties. The management committee recommended wind-down on 28 October, pending a partnership vote.

stories.t: 7 Fire Insurance Claims Mistakes That Can Delay Your Settlement
When More Than One Party Shares Responsibility for an Injury
From Bench to BigLaw And Why This New York Judge Chose Quinn Emanuel
stories.s: LawFuel publishes a firm-conducted interview announcing that John R. Higgitt, formerly an associate justice in the First Department of New York's Appellate Division, is joining Quinn Emanuel as a New York partner. Higgitt says he left the bench to gain advocacy experience and predicts more litigation over government regulation and AI. The piece is written by the firm and reproduces its interview.
e: New York State Supreme Court Appellate Division

stories.t: Sidley in talks to take Weil Paris office alongside heavyweight PE partners in London and Germany
GSK recruits new legal chief as long-serving GC prepares to step down
Weil’s shock collapse: What’s happening to current and future trainees?
Trainee solicitor and paralegal barred from law firms over sex offences
stories.s: Legal Cheek reports that the SRA has imposed section 43 orders on a former trainee solicitor, Toby Daniel Everden, and a former Ramsdens Solicitors paralegal, Anthony Sykes, after separate child sexual offence convictions. Everden was ordered to pay £600 towards costs, as was Sykes. Both cannot work in legal practice without the SRA's prior approval, according to the regulator's published decisions.

stories.t: Government backs “comprehensive review” of legal services regulation
‘Polluter pays’ means profession set to pay less for LeO
stories.s: The Legal Ombudsman's budget is set to rise 6.9 per cent to £22.8m in 2027-28 according to draft plans from the Office for Legal Complaints, but the levy on lawyers should fall as case fees rise. Complaints are forecast to reach 21,210 in 2027-28. Case fees would be £200, £750 or £1,500 depending on the stage, with £400 for missing the eight-week final response deadline.

stories.t: AML: Conveyancers “should report membership of developer panels”
Law firm can keep acting in dispute after partner swapped sides
stories.s: The High Court has ruled that Birketts can continue acting for a woman in a Tunbridge Wells property dispute, despite hiring Sebastian Burrows, a former partner at Stowe Family Law who had supervised the file for her ex-husband. Deputy High Court judge Nageena Khalique KC accepted Mr Burrows had no recollection of the case and found no real risk of disclosure. She said imputed knowledge alone did not bar the firm from acting.

stories.t: PE-backed personal injury deal leads trio of acquisitions
stories.s: Private equity-backed Express Solicitors has bought Manchester personal injury firm Ralli, bringing about 40 staff across, its fourth acquisition this year. Minster Law has opened a Cardiff office after acquiring RCN Law's employers' liability portfolio and some staff. Stone King has bought Sussex technology and media boutique Tacit Legal, with three partners joining.

stories.t: Regulate sole practices on evidence, not turnover
stories.s: Santosh Pandey, a solicitor going through SRA authorisation for his own practice, argues in a guest post that the proposed compliance officer rule for sole practices should be based on evidence and client money, not turnover. He says the SRA estimated 1,660 firms and 431 sole owner manager firms may need to act, and that the rule has never matched its reach. He proposes an independent accountant option.

stories.t: Fieldfisher rolls out Legora firm-wide
stories.s: Legal IT Insider reports that Fieldfisher has rolled out Legora firm-wide. The extract is only a site verification notice, so the scope, timing and terms of the rollout cannot be confirmed from the text available. The story concerns the legal AI platform Legora and a UK law firm.

stories.t: A&O Shearman ramps up AI push with five-year plan it says is worth $1.1bn
Hogan Lovells Cadwalader claims industry first with pro bono partnership deed pledge
Addleshaws steps up European expansion with 20-strong Taylor Wessing hire in Germany
Public inquiries 'too adversarial', Manchester Arena judge tells peers
stories.s: Sir John Saunders, who chaired the Manchester Arena Inquiry, told the House of Lords constitution committee that public inquiries are too adversarial, too long and too expensive. He suggested scope should be settled more tightly before an inquiry starts and that fewer lawyers should be involved. He also described a hearing held within three months of his first report to track progress on recommendations.

stories.t: LeO asks for 6.9% budget increase alongside new fee charges
stories.s: The Legal Ombudsman's draft business plan proposes a 6.9 per cent budget rise to £22.8m for 2027-28, with complaints expected above 21,000. The plan introduces tiered case fees of £200, £750 and £1,500 from next April, subject to Legal Services Board approval. LeO chief ombudsman Phil Cain says transformation means a more sustainable service, not more complaints processed.

stories.t: Buckles acquires London cross-border boutique
stories.s: Peterborough-based Buckles Law has acquired Miller Rosenfalck, a London boutique focused on cross-border work, particularly German and Scandinavian matters. Six lawyers join Buckles as partners, including Steen Rosenfalck, who founded Miller Rosenfalck in 2002. Buckles says the deal strengthens its employment, dispute resolution and corporate offer and adds an immigration service line. Duncan Jackson, Buckles chief executive, describes the firm as one of fewer than 50 B Corp certified law firms in the UK.

stories.t: Understanding Truck Accidents and When to Seek Legal Help in Texas
Bank of England increases interest rates for the first time in 3 years
Rightmove hearing ends with reserved judgment on opt-out position
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer reports that a Rightmove hearing has ended with judgment reserved on the opt-out position in the class action. The extract is mostly a page banner about Bank of England rate rises, so the article text is limited.

stories.t: Could the Bank of England hold interest rates today?
Confidence an ‘important benefit’ alongside speed to improve home buying
Over half of first-time buyers say saving had a negative impact on their lives
Firms risk falling foul of transparency compliance with 3 in 4 not displaying LPA fees
stories.s: Today's Wills and Probate reports that a large share of firms are not displaying their fees as required under the Legal Ombudsman's or LPA transparency rules, with three in four firms failing to show LPA fees. The extract is only a headline and a related link about LeO consulting on a new strategy. The full article should be checked for the survey source and sample.

stories.t: LeO to consult on new strategy as demand for its service outpaces capacity
Legal Services Board makes policy and performance appointments
stories.s: Today's Wills and Probate reports that the Legal Services Board has made policy and performance appointments. The extract is only a standfirst about firms failing to display LPA fees, so the names, roles and dates of the appointments cannot be confirmed from the text available. The same appointments are covered by the LSB's own release.

stories.t: Stronger consumer protection through more focused oversight
stories.s: The Legal Services Board has published its response to the Public Bodies Review, accepting all of its recommendations. It says it will focus oversight on areas of greatest consumer harm, reduce routine reporting for well-performing regulators and intensify oversight of the SRA after law firm failures. Chair Monisha Shah says the LSB will foster shared understanding of cross-sector risks. A consultation on its 2027-30 strategy is planned for autumn or winter 2026.

stories.t: Stronger oversight, better outcomes for consumers: LSB makes three senior appointments
stories.s: The Legal Services Board has appointed Shona Barton as Director, Regulatory Oversight, Sam Wood as Head of Performance and Oversight, and Atika Thomson as Head of Policy Development and Delivery. Shona and Sam start in January 2027 and Atika in December 2026. LSB chief executive Richard Orpin says the appointments will strengthen oversight of the eight frontline regulators.

stories.t: Policy paper: Government response to the Independent Public Bodies Review of the Legal Services Board
Simplifying AML Compliance: Aderant + First AML in Action
stories.s: Aderant and First AML are promoting a webinar, recorded on 4 November 2026 and lasting one hour, on a new integration between their products. The integration links client due diligence and AML checks within Aderant Expert and Expert Sierra, with audit-ready records. Speakers are Ian Emery of Aderant and Jack Abernethy of First AML, and the session includes a live demonstration.

stories.t: Protected: The AI Blind Spot in DSARs
stories.s: Elevate has published a protected post titled The AI Blind Spot in DSARs, so the extract shows only the title and a notice. The post concerns data subject access requests and AI, but the body is not visible.

stories.t: How many days does your client acceptance process take from partner yes to signed engagement letter?
stories.s: Intapp promotes a webinar on 10 November about Intapp Celeste, its Firm AI offering for accounting firms. The post argues that client acceptance delays between partner approval and signed engagement letter come from manual intake, conflicts and independence checks.

stories.t: The Hardest Part of Legal Tech Modernization Isn’t the New System
stories.s: Onit argues that replacing legacy legal systems is harder than adding new ones, and describes a sequenced approach of retiring broken systems first. It cites Medtronic, which chose Onit to replace legacy legal and contract management systems, launching separate-instance ELM and CLM deployments rather than one unified instance. According to Onit, the parallel approach let teams move independently under an aggressive timeline. The case study is presented in Onit's own words.

stories.t: AI in the courts: Time savings, divided opinions, and the risk of losing expertise
stories.s: Thomson Reuters CaseLines summarises the 2026 Survey of State Courts by the Thomson Reuters Institute and the National Center for State Courts, based on 116 court professionals and judges plus focus groups. It reports court staff expect AI to save about three hours a week this year, rising to 9.2 hours within five years. Respondents split 56 per cent to 44 per cent on whether AI will help or harm courts. Concerns include hallucinations and data security.

stories.t: European Digital Compliance: Key Digital Regulation & Compliance Developments (Q3 2026) | Morrison Foerster
stories.s: Morrison Foerster's European digital regulatory compliance team has published its Q3 2026 review of EU, UK and German digital rules. Topics include the EU AI Act transparency obligations, the proposed EU KIDS Act announced on 17 September 2026, the Cyber Resilience Act and the Data Act.

stories.t: Top Legal Tech, Service Providers, and Products in Canada | Readers’ Choice
stories.s: Canadian Lawyer has published the winners of its 2026 Readers' Choice Awards, listing providers by subcategory across legal technology, litigation support, research and related services. Thomson Reuters CoCounsel, Dye & Durham and Profile Legal Services are among the named winners.

stories.t: Canadian Lawyer unveils 2026 Readers’ Choice Award winners
stories.s: Canadian Lawyer has announced winners of its 2026 Readers' Choice Awards, covering 78 organisations across 17 categories. Thomson Reuters Canada won eight awards and Clio won six, according to the publication, with the vote held from 29 June to 24 July 2026.

stories.t: Voices of CLOC | Ty Lim
stories.s: CLOC has published a voices interview with Ty Lim, in which the piece poses the question of how much of the change management journey a legal technology vendor should own. The extract is brief, so the wider argument of the interview is not yet clear from the source. The item focuses on how legal departments and vendors share responsibility for adoption of new systems.

stories.t: A&O Shearman Pledges $1.1B To AI Buildout Led By Lawyers
stories.s: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech reports that A&O Shearman has pledged $1.1b to an AI buildout led by lawyers. The summary line gives no further detail on the scope, timing or structure of the commitment. The headline frames the investment as lawyer-led rather than technology-led, which may matter to how the firm positions its AI programme.

stories.t: Meet the Builders Already Rewriting the Rules
Addleshaw Goddard adds 20-strong Taylor Wessing team in Munich
Freeths expands Glasgow office to support growth
Imperfect Solutions: Botched Christa Pike execution invites fresh look at lethal injection
This state senator wrote music for ‘Dragon Ball Z;’ will he go ‘Super Saiyan’ as new Texas AG?
AI Does Wonders. But Keep Humans In The Loop
New Year, Bigger Paychecks For Associates At This Biglaw Firm
Paul, Weiss Would Like You To Stop Looking At Their Financials
20 Nonfiction Book Recommendations Perfect For Celebrating (Or Mourning) The Midterm Results
Quebec foster family group challenges unequal support for children under youth protection
Clio Wants To Bring AI to the Judiciary, But 50-State Survey Reveals Policies Differ in Whether They Allow It
stories.s: Clio is pushing into the judiciary, according to LawSites and LawNext, with hires Pablo Arredondo and Bridget McCormack and the acquisition of Learned Hand, an AI start-up for judges. Bob Ambrogi's 50-state survey finds judicial AI policies vary widely. Massachusetts bans judges and court staff from using generative AI for legal research and writing, while New York takes a more permissive approach. The survey relies on ChatGPT and Claude checks plus the author's own research.

stories.t: A&O Shearman announces new AI strategy, valued at $1.1bn over five years
stories.s: A&O Shearman has announced a five-year AI strategy worth $1.1bn, according to Legal Business. The firm says most of the sum will come from each practice committing 3 per cent of lawyers' time to developing AI tools and services across practice areas. The UK-headquartered firm frames the programme as specialising AI across its practices. The extract is mainly the article opening and the figures are the firm's own.

stories.t: MLT Digital
stories.s: MLT Digital, a performance marketing agency for law firms, describes its services in a company profile carried by Legal Futures. The agency says it covers search visibility including AI answer tools such as ChatGPT, brand and PR, and enquiry handling through its sister platform ReceptIO. It says it has worked with UK firms for more than 20 years. The text is a sponsored profile and gives no independent assessment of its results.

stories.t: Minister promises legal regulation 'reset' - in 2029
stories.s: The government has accepted in full the recommendations of the Richard Lloyd review of legal services regulation, according to The Law Society Gazette. Justice minister Sarah Sackman backs a 'reset' of the regulatory system. The Ministry of Justice must develop a new framework by 2029, with implementation in the next parliament. The government will also consider AI and lawtech in a comprehensive review. Law Society and Bar Council responses are reported.

stories.t: Client Fund Protection Rules for US Forex Brokers
CILEx Regulation responds to LSB reform plans
stories.s: CILEx Regulation has responded to the Legal Services Board's reform plans, which accept the recommendations of the Public Bodies Review led by Richard Lloyd. The LSB proposes earlier action on market risk, more targeted oversight of legal regulators, and better complaints handling. CILEx Regulation chair Jonathan Rees welcomed the report and called for a full review of the Legal Services Act 2007, arguing for a more risk-based regime.

stories.t: CLM Provider Leah Launches Self-Service AI Tool-Building Feature
stories.s: Leah, a contract lifecycle management provider, has launched Harness Builder, a feature that lets users build their own AI applications. According to the announcement, the tool is designed to let customers replace existing point solutions. The extract is brief and does not give pricing, availability dates or customer names.

stories.t: Retirement Talk For Alito And Thomas Gets Awkward After Democrats’ Senate Win
Making Yourself AI-Proof
Biglaw Associates Have Their Eyes On Raises And Even Bigger Bonuses
Are Law Firms Whistling Past The Graveyard? [Video]
stories.s: Above the Law reports that Weil, Gotshal and Manges has ended its 95-year run, and that correspondent Stephen Embry argues some law firm business practices amount to whistling past the graveyard as technology disrupts the industry. The item is a video piece using AI-generated dramatisation. It also links to a piece on whether in-house or outside counsel will control the AI relationship.

stories.t: International Court of Justice adds first UK judge in nearly a decade
stories.s: Canadian Lawyer reports that Dapo Akande, an Oxford public international law professor, has been elected a judge of the International Court of Justice, the first UK judge in nearly a decade. The UK government said the nine-year term was backed by most UN member states. The item also covers a Civil Justice Council working group report on AI in court documents.

stories.t: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader says it’s first global firm to put pro bono in constitution
Dentons welcomes employment and labour partner Laura Mensch in Calgary
CS Disco Hires Ex-Thomson Reuters CTO, Ex-Auros CMO
stories.s: CS Disco has hired a former chief technology officer of Thomson Reuters and a former chief marketing officer of Auros. The extract is only an outlet summary line, so the roles, start dates and reporting lines are not confirmed beyond the headline. Law360 Pulse Legal Tech carries the item.

stories.t: Ex-Eversheds Sutherland CEO Joins FTI Consulting In Atlanta
Stockholm-Based AI Contract Startup Juritas Raises €1.4M
Barnes & Thornburg Bolsters Real Estate Strength With Three-Partner Team Hire
Weil supports London business services staff with ‘Project Dunkirk’ rescue plan
Stris & Maher takes lead in filing AI copyright suits with 3 new suits v. Elon Musk’s company SpaceX Superintelligence
stories.s: Edward Lee's blog reports that Stris & Maher has filed three copyright suits against SpaceX Superintelligence over model development for xAI and SpaceX. The complaints argue that scanning lawfully owned books for AI training is not fair use, contrary to Bartz v. Anthropic. The blog's running total is now 164 cases.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Latest US Map of Copyright Suits v. AI cos. Total = 164
stories.s: Edward Lee's blog says its US map of copyright suits against AI companies now totals 164 cases. The update adds three new suits against SpaceX Superintelligence, named Cambronne, Chicken Soup and Cognella. The map is a commentator's tally rather than a court record.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Debevoise Data Blog : Your AI Agent Can Bind You: A Governance Framework for Autonomous Contracts
stories.s: Debevoise & Plimpton's data blog post, dated 4 November, is titled on a governance framework for autonomous AI contracts that can bind a company. The extract is only the outlet summary line, so the framework's contents are not visible here.

stories.t: Trustees facing declining banking options
Carter-Ruck welcomes Tomas Vail as partner
Gateley Legal wins double panel appointment
Major parsley producer wins at least £2.38m after factory fire exposes insurance risks facing British manufacturers
New safeguards for police facial recognition technology
Elite Achieves 100% Cloud Customer Retention as Law Firms Accelerate Financial Operations Modernization
stories.s: Thomson Reuters Elite says all firms that have migrated to its cloud have stayed with it, a 100 per cent retention rate. As of October 2026 it had 140 firms on the cloud, up 44 per cent year on year. Its 2026 report, produced with Law.com, reports a median 11 per cent fall in days sales outstanding. Named firms include Morton Fraser MacRoberts and Clark Hill.

stories.t: An Inside Look at Akin's Funds-Focused Development Lab
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Akin has set up a Funds Frontier Lab to build bespoke tools for its funds practice. The first project is a knowledge management tool. The extract is brief and does not give the lab's staffing or budget.

stories.t: Junior Lawyers Aren't Necessarily Driving In-House AI Adoption
stories.s: A Pinsent Masons report found that 31 per cent of in-house legal professionals surveyed said more junior colleagues were driving AI adoption. The finding challenges assumptions about who leads technology change in the profession. The extract is a short summary and gives no further survey detail.

stories.t: A&O Shearman Commits Around $1B In Lawyer Hours to AI Development
stories.s: A&O Shearman has committed around $1bn of lawyer hours to AI development, according to a Legal Tech Monitor report. The report describes it as among the largest law firm investments in AI so far. Big Law firms are increasingly building bespoke platforms, the report says. The extract gives no further detail on the scope of the commitment.

stories.t: Republicans Aren’t the Only Losers in This Week’s Elections: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.s: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today post reviews the US midterm elections and argues that data centres and AI were losers. It cites a New York Times report that voters in 40 of 41 local ballot initiatives limited data centre development. He expects Democrats to bring new AI bills next year, which he says a Republican president may veto. This is commentary.

stories.t: The Importance of an AI Policy Checklist: Artificial Intelligence Best Practices
stories.s: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today post reviews a Cimplifi article on the value of an AI policy checklist for law firms and corporate legal departments. The checklist aims to turn confidentiality and supervision commitments into everyday decisions, such as uploading deposition testimony or charging clients for AI-assisted research. Cimplifi is a sponsor of the blog.

stories.t: Biglaw Salaries Are Going Up, Up, Up — See Also
It All Hinges On Judgment. And Human Connections.
Saskatchewan Legal Profession Amendment Act to boost agent regulation
stories.s: Saskatchewan's government introduced the Legal Profession Amendment Act, 2026 on 4 November, tightening oversight of agents, non-lawyers who regularly appear for clients before courts and tribunals. The Law Society of Saskatchewan would gain authority to regulate agent activity. The bill also creates a separate process for lawyers with health or capacity problems, outside disciplinary proceedings. Justice minister Tim McLeod and Law Society executive director Tim Brown both welcomed the changes, according to the report.

stories.t: Budget 2026 to fund translation of court rulings, tax reforms that impact lawyers, victims’ services
stories.s: Canada's federal budget, tabled on 5 November by Prime Minister Mark Carney, proposes C$58 billion between 2026 and 2031 to reduce the court translation backlog and help the Federal Court with caseloads. A tax change would let business-income earners, including lawyers, pay one instalment a year from 2028. Funding is also set for victims' services and youth custody.

stories.t: 8 Best Places to Hire Virtual Paralegals in 2026: Costs, Experience, and Reviews Compared
NZ Law News – TV producer Alexander Breingan’s appeal dismissed
Yale Professor’s “Why Law Firms Collapse” Paper Takes Renewed Interest in Wake of Weil
stories.s: LawFuel reports renewed interest in Professor John Morley's paper Why Law Firms Collapse after the announced closure of Weil, Gotshal and Manges. Morley argues partner ownership makes firms prone to sudden withdrawals, based on a study of three dozen failures. Morley is at Yale Law School and was quoted by Reuters and Bloomberg.

stories.t: Legal AI Company Seeks Legal Teams to Build Their Own AI Systems – No Developers
stories.s: Leah, a London-based agentic AI company formerly known as ContractPodAi, has launched Harness Builder, a capability within its Maestro platform. According to the launch statement dated 5 November, business users can describe objectives in plain language and have the platform build governed AI applications for legal, contracting and procurement teams. Leah says it connects to existing enterprise systems. LawFuel notes that independent evidence of performance is still needed.

stories.t: Mixed response to government review of legal services regulation
Barrister reported to BSB over “hateful rhetoric towards Jews”
stories.s: The Campaign Against Antisemitism has referred barrister Usha Sood, head of Trent Chambers, to the Bar Standards Board over social media comments on Israel and Gaza. Ms Sood denies being hateful or anti-Jewish. The BSB annual report shows social media complaints more than doubled to 279 in 2025-26, and total reports rose to 3,439.

stories.t: LSB promises tougher scrutiny and ‘significant’ shake-up in response to Public Bodies Review
stories.s: The Legal Services Board has promised tougher scrutiny and a significant shake-up of its work in response to the Public Bodies Review led by Richard Lloyd. The LSB says it will focus more on regulatory oversight. The article is a headline-level item in the extract; the Lloyd review found the LSB had lost its way in recent years.

stories.t: Fears for sustainability of conveyancing as research suggests fees are down 3.5% year on year
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer's headline reports fears for conveyancing sustainability, citing research that fees fell 3.5 per cent year on year. The extract shows an unrelated LSB headline, so the article body was not available to confirm the research source. The subject is the economics of conveyancing practice.

stories.t: Members body releases digital sales packs and logbook guidance to support reform roadmap
Conveyancing Association focus on role conveyancers play in the home buying and selling process at upcoming annual conference
stories.s: The Conveyancing Association will focus on the role conveyancers play in home buying and selling at its upcoming annual conference. The extract provided is a related headline about the LSB review and does not describe the conference programme, so the speakers and dates are not confirmed from this text.

stories.t: Half of adults say they would accept AI involvement in will drafting
More Flexibility, Faster Payments: What’s New with 8am LawPay + Aderant Expert
stories.s: Aderant and 8am have promoted a webinar recorded on 5 November 2026 on updates to the LawPay and Aderant Expert integration. The updates include URL-based pre-filled payment pages and a coming BillBlast integration for paying emailed invoices. The speakers are product and sales staff from both companies.

stories.t: More Flexibility, Faster Payments: What’s New with 8am LawPay + Aderant Expert
stories.s: Aderant and 8am have promoted a webinar recorded on 5 November 2026 on updates to the LawPay and Aderant Expert integration. The updates include URL-based pre-filled payment pages and a coming BillBlast integration for paying emailed invoices. The speakers are product and sales staff from both companies.

stories.t: Simplifying AML Compliance: Aderant + First AML in Action
stories.s: Aderant and First AML have promoted a webinar, recorded on 4 November 2026, on their integration for anti-money laundering checks within Aderant Expert and Expert Sierra. The session covers client due diligence, audit records and a live demonstration. Speakers are from Aderant's EMEA team and First AML.

stories.t: How Legal Teams Budget for Shocks: Cash, Capacity, or Process
stories.s: Axiom's 2027 In-House Legal Budget Report, based on 510 respondents, found legal teams mainly budget for uncertainty through flexible budgeting, flexible talent and budget buffers. Scenario-based budgets were rare, chosen by 7 to 8 per cent. UK teams lean towards cash reserves for political risk, with 47 per cent increasing buffers, according to the post.

stories.t: Dye & Durham Announces Support Agreements with Plantro and EdgePoint, Strengthening Governance with New Appointments
stories.s: Dye & Durham has signed support agreements with shareholders Plantro and EdgePoint, which together hold about 36 per cent of shares. Former CEO Matthew Proud, Lee Matheson and Peter Brimm join the board, and Patrick Dennis is named a board observer. The litigation between Plantro and the company will be dismissed. Interim CEO Todd Schulte says the search for a permanent CEO continues.

stories.t: Data Subject Request
stories.s: Elevate's blog has posted an item titled Data Subject Request. The extract is only the outlet's standard line, so the post's content and its subject area within data protection practice are not visible here.

stories.t: Everlaw Workflows Turns Your Best Strategy into a Repeatable Standard
stories.s: Everlaw has launched Workflows, a visual builder for multi-stage document review that routes documents, assigns reviewers and runs quality and privilege checks. According to Everlaw, only users with Workflow Admin permission can publish workflows, and teams can copy them to new matters. Everlaw says its AI tools such as Coding Suggestions are planned for later releases.

stories.t: Spellbook's October Product Spotlight
stories.s: Spellbook has published a roundup of nine product updates for October. Changes include Word add-in support for tables, Word comments and list formatting, AI-generated comments on redlines, grouped and team-wide Playbook rules, admin usage dashboards and ACM features for deal ownership, Slack sync and a contract request portal. The vendor says the Word add-in now keeps inline formatting through edits.

stories.t: AI agents went stale in just four months
stories.s: Syntheia, which runs an AI certification course for in-house teams, argues that AI agents have moved from projects to simple chat prompts in four months. It describes in-house teams vibe-coding custom tools, and says the question is now which workflows are worth automating. The post is opinion from a vendor that runs training.

stories.t: What customers are saying about CoCounsel Legal
stories.s: Thomson Reuters CaseLines has published customer testimonials on the new CoCounsel Legal, drawn from attorneys at small and Am Law 100 firms, in-house teams, courts and public defenders. Customers say the tool draws on Westlaw and Practical Law, needs no prompt engineering, and that lawyers still review output. Named users include Duane Morris, Polsinelli and Teladoc Health.

stories.t: DWF supports Sustainable Investments Group growth
555 Expert witness survey highlights key trends
stories.s: Bond Solon, with the Law Society Gazette, has published its expert witness survey, conducted online from 2 to 25 September 2026 with 555 respondents. The survey reports pressure on fees, payment delays, AI use and standards, and says respondents want clearer AI protocols and some form of accreditation or regulation.

stories.t: The new client: Claude
stories.s: A junior solicitor writing in Solicitors Journal describes how clients increasingly consult AI before instructing lawyers, bringing challenges around trust, privilege and costs. The column says uploading confidential documents to public AI platforms may compromise confidentiality and privilege, and that clients sometimes ask for second opinions from AI on counsel's advice.

stories.t: Law Society of Scotland informs MPs on Lord Advocate inquiry
stories.s: The Law Society of Scotland told the Scottish Affairs Committee that any reform of the Lord Advocate's dual role must be evidence-led and consulted on widely. Michael Clancy, its Director of Law Reform, gave oral evidence on 4 November. The Society has not taken a final position and says its inquiry evidence could inform Lord Boyd's Scottish Government review.

stories.t: New law helps young people find jobs
Harvey + Legora IPO Plans, A&O $1.1bn, Legal Innovators NY
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer's weekly wrap reports that Harvey and Legora are each reported to be in early IPO discussions with advisers. Legora's spokesperson said it does not comment on speculation, though CEO Max Junestrand has long said he wants to list one day. The piece links possible listings to a risk of AI valuation correction and notes Big Tech moves into legal.

stories.t: The mentorship questions law students should ask during recruitment
Litera and filerskeepers Bridge the Gap Between Global Retention Requirements and Records Governance
Introducing SimpleDocs 360: AI-Native Contract Lifecycle Management
stories.s: SimpleDocs, the Miami provider of AI contract solutions and parent of Law Insider, has launched SimpleDocs 360, an AI-native contract lifecycle management platform. According to the company, it combines three products, SimpleAI, Workflow and Repository, and integrates with tools including Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft Word and DocuSign. CEO Preston Clark says it was built for the AI era. Hundreds of enterprise customers are said to already use SimpleDocs.

stories.t: A&O Shearman to devote billable hours to building AI tools as part of $1 billion investment
stories.s: A&O Shearman plans to put more than 5 per cent of annual revenue into AI over five years, a $1.1bn (£800m) investment. Lawyers in every practice will be asked to set aside at least 3 per cent of billable time to help build specialist AI tools. Global managing partner Hervé Ekué says the firm wants lawyers at the centre of AI development rather than relying only on ready-made products.

stories.t: ‘I think my supervisor is trying to sabotage my career. Should I quit?’
Startup Corner: Lawfecta looks to AI to solve law firms’ legal talent needs
stories.s: Legal IT Insider's startup corner profiles Lawfecta, which is said to use AI to address law firms' legal talent needs. The extract available is only a site verification page, so the substance of the piece cannot be confirmed from what was supplied. The story is likely a profile of an early-stage company rather than a deal or launch.

stories.t: Addleshaw Goddard adds McDermott PE partner trio as hiring push gathers pace
‘A real sense of loss’: Leaders reflect after closure of firm
stories.s: Berwins Solicitors, a Harrogate firm founded 40 years ago with around 40 staff, has entered administration after filing a notice of appointment. Managing director Danielle Day confirmed the appointment on LinkedIn. No reasons for the closure have been given, and accounts to June 2025 showed net assets of almost £300,000.

stories.t: We will change - but it will cost you, says LSB
stories.s: The Legal Services Board has welcomed an independent review by Richard Lloyd of legal services regulation, which the government has accepted in full. LSB chair Monisha Shah says the regulator will set out a 2027-30 strategy and warns that change needs strategic investment, with a budget consultation to follow. Blind Justice UK criticises the review for not covering the SRA or setting a timetable.

stories.t: In depth: Bond Solon/Gazette Expert Witness Survey 2026 - key takeaways
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette, with Bond Solon, publishes key findings from its 2026 expert witness survey of 555 experts. AI use has risen, with 12 per cent saying they use it regularly and 23 per cent occasionally, while 73 per cent cite over-reliance on AI as a concern. Most respondents back formal regulation of expert witnesses, by 51 per cent to fewer than one in four opposed.

stories.t: AI use by litigants in person adding to courts burden, LCJ warns
stories.s: The lady chief justice, Baroness Carr of Walton-on-the-Hill, says in her third annual judiciary report that litigants in person are increasingly using AI to build claims, placing significant demands on court staff and judges. The report, covering October 2025 to September 2026, says the Court of Appeal Criminal Division is preparing guidance on AI in grounds of appeal and that oversight of AI use will remain judge-led.

stories.t: Claims firm's losses double to £4.8m - but caseload 'exceptionally strong'
stories.s: Manchester claims firm Veritas Solicitors reports that its operating losses more than doubled to £4.8m for the year to 29 November 2025, with turnover down 8 per cent to around £9m. Its members' report says the current caseload could yield £134m if settled. The accounts show £63.9m owed, net liabilities of £30m and a debtor, I Quote, that says it cannot make further payments.

stories.t: Al-Ateeqi v Kuwait Investment Authority: EAT upholds state immunity in sovereign wealth fund whistleblowing claim
New PTAB Challenge Filed in IPR2027-00030 Involving Shining 3D Tech
Speech by Mrs Justice Joanna Smith: Artificial Intelligence and Expert Evidence – Opportunities, Risks and Responsibilities
Watch the webinar about new guidance and materials for short notice applications in public law family cases
Former state official charged with tampering bar exam results
stories.s: Arkansas prosecutors have charged Nancie Givens, former executive director of the Arkansas Supreme Court's Office of Professional Programs, with 65 felony counts. The state supreme court says an investigation found irregularities in bar exam results from 2020 to 2025, with 11,400 files deleted or unavailable.

stories.t: 2 BigLaw firms face proposed class actions over cyber breaches
Biglaw’s Best-Paid Partners Now Live In Silicon Valley, Sorry Manhattan
Why MCP Could Be A Hero For Your Lean Legal Team
