stories.s: Above the Law is promoting a webinar on 12 November, hosted with Generate and Brightflag, on using Model Context Protocol (MCP) in lean legal operations teams. Michelle Garza of Generate and Anna Richards of Brightflag will cover how MCP works, answering spend and vendor questions, and managing AI tool permissions.

stories.t: Judges Shouldn’t Avoid Difficult Decisions By Pushing For Settlements
Dentons’ new global practice heads include four across Toronto, Vancouver
Voir Dire: Law360 Pulse's Weekly Quiz
US Charges 3 Over $129M AI Scam Using Fake UK Lawyers
stories.s: US prosecutors have charged three people over an alleged $129m artificial intelligence scam that used fake UK lawyers, according to a Law360 Pulse Legal Tech headline. The extract is only a summary line, so details of the charges, defendants and the scheme are not available here.

stories.t: Cravath makes rare London partner promotion amid 11-strong round
stories.s: Cravath has promoted Lawrence Verhelst, a London counsel focused on finance and capital markets, to partner as part of an 11-strong round. Legal Business says it is the firm's largest partner promotions round since 2020. Verhelst joined as an associate in 2014 and has been European counsel since late 2021.

stories.t: Catching the pro bono bug: Lloyds and Societe Generale among new sign-ups as In House Pro Bono Pledge reaches 25
Full details: the five-partner Weil team joining Kirkland with Ramona Nee
stories.s: Legal Business reports that Ramona Nee, a Boston-based private equity partner and co-head of Weil's US PE practice, is joining Kirkland & Ellis in the New Year with five further partners from Weil's M&A and finance groups. The team totals 40 lawyers, according to the report.

stories.t: Harvey held preliminary meetings with Latham advisors over potential listing
stories.s: Legal Business understands that Harvey has held preliminary meetings with its regular advisers Latham & Watkins about a possible future listing. The report says the talks were preliminary and that Harvey has no imminent IPO plans. The discussions were first reported by Business Insider.

stories.t: Kirkland hires 40-strong Weil team led by Ramona Nee
stories.s: Kirkland & Ellis has hired a 40-lawyer PE, M&A and debt finance team from Weil, led by Ramona Nee, according to Kirkland's announcement. The group joins in January 2027 and includes six partners. Kirkland's executive committee chair Jon Ballis praised the hires.

stories.t: Slaughters and HSF Kramer join legal line-up for Anthropic IPO
Cravath promotes one in London in 11-strong partner round
stories.s: Nonbillable reports that Cravath has promoted London lawyer Lawrence Verhelst to partner in an 11-strong global round, taking its London partnership to eight. The firm's average profit per partner was $7.2m last year, per The American Lawyer. Verhelst joins on 1 January.

stories.t: Peers condemn use of 'Henry VIII' powers in jury trial bill
stories.s: A House of Lords Delegated Powers committee has criticised the Courts and Tribunals Bill for giving ministers power, under Clause 3(5), to add offences to the list tried without a jury through secondary legislation. The committee wants that change made in primary legislation. The bill goes to a Lords bill committee on Tuesday.
e: House of Lords Delegated Powers and Regulatory Reform Committee

stories.t: Minesoft Origin vs PatSnap vs Questel Orbit: Which Platform Fits Your Team?
Form: Make a claim with others to an employment tribunal: Form ET1A
stories.s: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has uploaded a Welsh translated version of Form ET1A, used to make a joint claim to an employment tribunal. The form page was updated on 6 November 2026, following an amended English form dated 30 October 2026.

stories.t: Ivo becomes Official Legal AI Partner of the 76ers and Devils
FTI Consulting hires former Eversheds Sutherland CEO
stories.s: LegalTechTalk reports that FTI Consulting has appointed former Eversheds Sutherland chief executive Mark Wasserman as a Senior Managing Director. He will advise law firms and corporate legal departments.

stories.t: Subpoenas Are Coming: Washington Law Firms Are Getting Ready For A Congressional Probe Boom
stories.s: Above the Law reports that Democratic wins in both chambers will bring congressional investigations, with lawyers in Washington preparing. Brian Nieves and Mark Epley expect more investigators, and Cooley's Susanne Grooms warned the volume could double. Nine law firms that agreed to provide $940 million in free legal services to Trump may be targets, according to the piece.

stories.t: Harmeet Heads For The Hills
From Biglaw To Boutique: Tyka’s Co-Chair Shares His Thoughts On Building A New Firm
stories.s: Above the Law interviews Ben Eggert, co-chair of Tyka, an insurance boutique launched by 21 attorneys from Wiley Rein. Eggert says the firm brought over 50 clients and 1,500 matters and describes the work of setting up document management and billing. The interview covers client retention through the transition.

stories.t: Bar Exam Official Charged With 65 Felonies, Accused Of Playing Robin Hood With Test Scores
iManage Puts A Firm’s Institutional Knowledge To Work For Agentic AI
stories.s: iManage has described its next generation platform, released in October, which adds AI features to its document management system. Paul Walker, Global Solutions Director, demonstrated for Above the Law how a calendar Get Ready button builds meeting briefings, how Playbooks check batches of documents against review standards, and how citations link back to source documents. iManage says it stores about 30 billion documents for 3,500 customers.

stories.t: Grain inspectors and graders' union activity falls under derivative federal jurisdiction: SCC
Legal Tech Roundup: Manifest, Litera, Cellebrite, DealCloser
stories.s: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech has published a roundup covering Manifest, Litera, Cellebrite and DealCloser. The extract is only the outlet summary line, so the content of each item cannot be confirmed from this text.

stories.t: Attys Can Curb AI Error Fallout With Candor, Accountability
Kirkland Hires the Woman Who Was Meant to Save Weil
Buchalter Elevates Twelve Attorneys to Partner in 2026
stories.s: Buchalter says it has promoted 12 attorneys to partner across 10 practice groups and seven offices in 2026. Adam Bass, the firm's President and CEO, praised the internal promotions. The release profiles each new partner's practice.

stories.t: Emmerich Newspaper v. OpenAI suit in Mississippi conditionally transferred to MDL before Judge Stein
stories.s: Edward Lee reports that the Emmerich Newspapers suit against OpenAI and Microsoft, filed in the Southern District of Mississippi, has been conditionally transferred to the multidistrict litigation before Judge Stein. A second Mississippi newspaper suit, Boone Newsmedia v. Microsoft, remains in that district.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Phil Rosen voluntarily dismisses Illinois suit v. Sundar Pichai but plans on refiling in California
stories.s: Phil Rosen has voluntarily dismissed a copyright shareholder suit against Google chief executive Sundar Pichai filed in the Northern District of Illinois. Rosen reportedly plans to refile in the Northern District of California, according to the commentary.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Jensen Huang moves to dismiss copyright shareholder derivative suit of Berliner
stories.s: NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang and other NVIDIA officers and directors have moved to dismiss a shareholder derivative suit brought by Berliner. The suit rests on a novel theory of copyright risk, according to the commentary.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Washington Law Firms Gear up for Looming Democratic Probes // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley reports that partner Susanne Grooms spoke to Reuters about a likely surge in congressional investigations after Democrats won both chambers in the midterms, and said the volume could double. The post links to the Reuters piece and lists earlier press mentions.

stories.t: Travis LeBlanc Named to Forbes’ Inaugural America’s Top Lawyers for AI List // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley says Forbes has named its partner Travis LeBlanc to the inaugural America's Top Lawyers for AI list. LeBlanc co-chairs Cooley's global cyber, data and privacy practice and advises on cybersecurity, data privacy, telecommunications and emerging technology regulation. According to the announcement, Forbes selected honorees through a multistage editorial process assessing the significance and complexity of their AI-related work, broader practice and thought leadership.

stories.t: HHS Finalizes Deregulatory Overhaul of ONC Health IT Certification Program | Morrison Foerster
stories.s: Morrison Foerster reports that HHS, through ONC, has finalised the HTI-5 rule, which substantially cuts requirements under the ONC Health IT Certification Program. The firm is summarising the regulator's action for its healthcare readers.

stories.t: AI Model Governance for Legal Teams: A Working Framework
stories.s: Neota Logic publishes a guide to AI model governance for general counsel and legal operations leaders. It sets out what a defensible framework contains, including an inventory, use-case classification, deployment controls, versioned records and monitoring. The guide cites the ABA technology section and a State Bar generative AI framework.

stories.t: Sarah Irwin On The AI Issue GCs Should Fix First | Summize
stories.s: Sarah Irwin of ITGC, a community for in-house legal teams, writes on Summize's site about AI accuracy for general counsel. She cites a survey of 82 European in-house leaders in which 70 per cent named accuracy as their top AI concern. She also cites Summize's AI Fluency Report, based on 505 US in-house professionals, which found 14.5 per cent connect AI to approved internal knowledge.

stories.t: Time | Track Every Billable Hour, Automatically | Elite
stories.s: Thomson Reuters Elite promotes Always-On Time, which it says captures 10 to 15 per cent more billable time. A UK partner describes moving from handwritten notes to recording a full day. The page is vendor marketing with a customer testimonial.

stories.t: Proforma | Turn Proforma Review into a Billing Accelerator | Elite
stories.s: Thomson Reuters Elite promotes Proforma and cites its 2026 Cloud Results Report, which draws on more than 120 law firms. The report says firms that moved finance operations to the cloud cut days sales outstanding and shortened month-end close. The page is vendor marketing.

stories.t: Copyright Suits Over AI Training Continue With Latest Surge Against Meta
Juritas Raises 1.4M Pre-Seed for Contract Intelligence Platform
Legaltech Rundown: Harvey Launches Litigation Tool, Agiloft Debuts New AI Agents, and More
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor's weekly rundown covers recent legal technology product launches and partnerships. The headline names Harvey launching a litigation tool and Agiloft debuting new AI agents. The extract is only the opening line, so details of each launch come from the full article.

stories.t: Harvey Holds Early Talks Over Potential IPO
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports that Harvey, the legal AI company, has held preliminary discussions with Latham & Watkins about a possible IPO. The outlet says no flotation is imminent. The extract is a single summary line and rests on reported talks.

stories.t: The Kitchen Sink for November 6, 2026: Legal Tech Trends
stories.s: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today kitchen sink for 6 November 2026 collects around ten stories with brief comments. Topics include a count of 2,266 AI hallucination cases, a Californian data breach register where social engineering is a common cause, and a judge's remarks on grace toward opposing counsel. The post is commentary on other reports.

stories.t: How Appealing Weekly Roundup
Squire Patton, Baker McKenzie Hit With Data Breach Suits
Slater & Gordon Bounces Back With $46 Million Profit After Years of Financial Turmoil
‘Start telling us now about AI use’, top judge urges experts
stories.s: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith told the Bond Solon Expert Witness Conference that experts should declare AI use now, before a rule requires it. She co-chaired the Civil Justice Council working group whose report last week recommended a declaration where AI shaped the substantive content of an expert report. She said the duties of independence and objectivity have not changed.

stories.t: Your AI can now update the deal, not just read it
stories.s: Legatics says its MCP connector now supports write actions, letting connected AI assistants create matters, update checklist items, add comments and reassign work in live deal files. Changes sit under existing user permissions and appear in the audit trail.

stories.t: Bonus Wrap: Harvey, Jus Mundi, LI NY +
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer's bonus round-up covers several legal technology and law firm items from the week. Akin and its Funds Frontier Lab launched Living Fund File, a fund-lifecycle knowledge product. eDiscovery company DISCO hired Mich Razon as chief technology officer, and Johann Wrede as chief marketing officer. CLM provider Leah launched Harness Builder, and Harvey launched a litigation and investigations capability built on its fact graph. Agiloft added AI agents, and Orbital launched Scots law workflows piloted with Pinsent Masons.

stories.t: FTC’s $49.75 Million Deal With Progress Residential Signals Rising Scrutiny of Rental Pricing
Ten questions law firm leaders are pondering right now – plus one off the wall
stories.s: Simon P Marshall, founder of TBD Marketing, writes in LawFuel that law firm leaders at a conference were focused on the possible dissolution of Weil, not on the formal agenda. He says TBD's analysis of five months of LinkedIn posts found far more references to growth and awards than to pricing or restructuring. The column then sets out ten questions leaders are asking, including how to keep rainmakers.

stories.t: Court finds law firm negligent over “simple human error”
stories.s: A High Court judge sitting in Manchester has ordered Ratio Law to pay £100,000 plus interest to MPP (Services) Ltd. The firm admitted that a partner, Gisela Alberici, accidentally deleted the sum secured from a draft legal charge on a property, leaving it void. The judge described Ms Alberici as an unimpressive witness who gave the matter only the bare minimum of attention. The article is a court report on the claim.

stories.t: Billionaire Hedge Fund Boss Sues Top Tax KC After HMRC Defeat
In depth: LLPs dodged a bullet in the budget - but HMRC is on their case
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that HMRC is putting professional services firms under aggressive scrutiny following the Supreme Court's BlueCrest ruling on LLP members' self-employment status. Boston Consulting Group's UK arm is reported to be among those targeted, and it says it is in discussion with HMRC. PKF Francis Clark's Andrew Allen warns the tax at stake could be material for law firms, and outlines capital and remuneration steps firms are reviewing.

stories.t: No costs for solicitor who left LiP in “intolerable position”
stories.s: Mr Justice Fordham has refused the London Borough of Tower Hamlets any costs for a judicial review claim after its solicitor, Mr Onuba, served key documents very late on a litigant in person, Mabel Abdul, who is acting for her disabled four-year-old son. The judge said the council had failed to acknowledge its defaults and that the position placed on Ms Abdul was intolerable. The council may not rely on the late documents.

stories.t: Latest US Map of Copyright Suits v. AI companies. Total = 166
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Technology & Commercial Transactions | Travers Smith
stories.s: Travers Smith describes its commercial, intellectual property and technology team, saying it advises across many sectors on transactions and sets out its service approach. The text is firm marketing for its practice and contains no deal or date. It is a law firm describing its own services.

stories.t: Calls for electronic bills review grow
stories.s: The Solicitors Journal reports that Senior Costs Judge Jason Rowley has called for a review of the electronic bill of costs at a roundtable run by the Association of Costs Lawyers. ACL vice-chair Victoria Morrison-Hughes and silk Nick Bacon KC also comment. The ACL says it will help with reform.

stories.t: Legal problems cost businesses time, money
Legal aid system for brain-damaged children deemed unjust
stories.s: Lawyers at the Association of Personal Injury Lawyers say Scotland's legal aid rules for families pursuing compensation for brain-damaged children are unjust. Under current rules both parents' finances are assessed. APIL has responded to a Scottish Government consultation on modernising legal aid, arguing that only the child's resources should be considered.

stories.t: Cameron Half strengthens Dorsey’s London office
DISCO Announces Senior Hires to Accelerate AI for Litigators | DISCO
stories.s: DISCO, the litigation technology company listed on the NYSE, says it has appointed Mich Razon as chief technology officer and Johann Wrede as chief marketing officer, both joining on 2 November 2026. Razon was previously at Thomson Reuters and Wrede at Auros. DISCO also cites growth in its AI platform and four Am Law 50 firms in a pilot.

stories.t: Legal AI ROI? Measure & benchmark your team's progress. Real-time exercise to generate your AI Maturity report.
stories.s: Factor, a vendor, invites in-house legal teams to a live working session with TITANS Legal's Peter Duffy to complete the AI Maturity Index and receive a personalised report. The index covers five dimensions and compares results with a market benchmark. The session is promoted as a registration event.

stories.t: Legal AI ROI? Measure your firm’s progress
stories.s: Factor invites law firms to a live working session with TITANS Legal's Peter Duffy to work through the AI Maturity Index and receive a personalised report. The law firm version covers six dimensions, including AI's effect on pricing and profitability. The event is promoted as a registration.

stories.t: From Cautious to Confident: AI Training for Legal Professionals [Webinar Recording]
stories.s: Factor, a contract management vendor, has published a recording of a webinar led by Alex Denniston and hosted with LegalOps.com. The session covers prompting, checking AI outputs against sources and assessing when AI agents need guardrails. The page promotes Factor's Sensemaker Academy training.

stories.t: Legal AI agents for end-to-end legal work | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes agents that build their own legal specialists and tools for each task, then carry out work end to end in Word documents. Examples include drafting to signature, due diligence and template migration. Each stage passes an independent reviewer. The page is vendor marketing with product examples.

stories.t: AI contract drafting in your house style | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes its contract drafting feature, which creates contracts, letters and policies from scratch or from a firm's templates. It says the tool fills placeholders from instructions or documents and keeps a requirement checklist. The page is vendor product marketing.

stories.t: AI contract review and redlining you can send | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes AI contract review that checks documents clause by clause against a customer's playbooks and produces a risk-rated issues table with suggested fixes. It says tracked changes can be accepted or rejected in one step and that it works with Word, PDF, Excel and image files. The page is vendor marketing.

stories.t: AI contract playbooks built from your own deals | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes a feature that builds a contract playbook from a company's past agreements, setting out standard positions, fallbacks and risk levels. The page says a playbook is held in one library and applied in a set order. It cites an internal benchmark score of 9.0 out of 10 against 5.9 for a general AI assistant, which the vendor itself reports.

stories.t: AI contract negotiation from your own playbook | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes a negotiation feature that summarises each new contract draft, answers counterparty markup from a playbook and tracks open points. The vendor says users can reply to comments and tracked changes in Word and send rounds from the project. The page is product marketing.

stories.t: AI legal research with every source cited | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes its legal research product, which says it reads legislation, regulators and courts across 15 jurisdiction groups and shows the source and retrieval date for each answer. It says only approved sources can verify a figure. The page is the vendor's own marketing copy.

stories.t: How Genie’s legal AI agents plan and do the work | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes how its legal AI agents plan and carry out work. It says each task goes through four phases, each passed by an independent reviewer, and that users can steer the work. The page cites customer quotes and ISO 27001 certification, which the vendor says it has held since 2019.

stories.t: AI document editor that keeps your Word formatting | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes an AI document editor that edits a user's original Word file and writes changes as native tracked changes, keeping formatting and numbering. The page says every edit saves a version that can be restored. The material is vendor product marketing.

stories.t: Self-verified legal AI you can check line by line | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI says its legal AI passes requirements, plans and outputs through an independent reviewer and traces each figure to a source. It says a figure is marked verified only when read from an approved source. It cites an internal benchmark on an NEC4 subcontract review, which the vendor describes itself.

stories.t: Legal workspaces for every team and client | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes its legal workspaces, with company, shared, members-only and private spaces, plus client-based spaces for law firms and project boards by status. The page says removing someone from a members-only space ends their access at once. It is vendor product marketing and includes customer quotes supplied by the vendor.

stories.t: AI contract repository that organises itself | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes a contract repository that reads uploaded templates, playbooks, signed agreements and policies and files them into five libraries. The page says duplicate uploads are stored once and documents can be moved between team spaces. It is vendor product marketing.

stories.t: AI contract data extraction into one table | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes a feature that reads every contract in a store and fills a single table, with one row per document and one column per question. Users can add plain-English questions and re-read individual rows. The page is vendor product marketing and includes customer quotes that the vendor supplies.

stories.t: Microsoft Word add-in for AI contract review | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes a Microsoft Word add-in that opens a side panel in the document, with two-way sync between Word and the Genie platform. Users can edit, review, explain or summarise, and run a red, amber and green risk review. Sign-in uses Office accounts.

stories.t: Legal AI for Gmail, Outlook, Drive and SharePoint | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI describes a feature set that lets users search Google Drive, Gmail, Outlook, OneDrive and SharePoint from its conversation interface, import only chosen files, and send finished work from their own email accounts. SharePoint access may need IT admin approval. The page is vendor marketing.

stories.t: E-signature with DocuSign and Adobe Acrobat Sign | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI says its platform can prepare signature requests from a matter project inside a customer's own Adobe Acrobat Sign account, and can place signature and date fields for DocuSign. The page is vendor marketing and describes the user sending the request. Security claims include ISO 27001 and zero data retention with OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.t: Legal templates for any contract, policy or deed | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI has published guidance on UK legal drafting, covering the separate legal systems of England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, employment status, confidentiality clauses, liability limits and data protection policies. The piece is general legal explainer content from a vendor promoting its templates. It is not a news event.

stories.t: Legal AI research since 2017, papers and data | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI's page describes a research project funded by a £1.5m UKRI grant to a consortium of Barclays, Withers, the University of Oxford and Imperial College London. The project aimed to explain machine learning decisions and to de-identify legal contracts. The page is the vendor's own account and gives no completion date in the extract.

stories.t: Legal AI for Consultancies: Win Work Faster | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI's page is headed Legal AI for Consultancies and frames its tools as a way to win work faster. The extract only shows an unrelated guide to drafting a consulting agreement, so the product claims cannot be checked from the extract. The page is vendor marketing.

stories.t: Legal AI for Consumer Services: Terms at Scale | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI, a legal AI vendor, markets its product to consumer-services businesses for drafting, reviewing and negotiating terms, subscription and vendor agreements. The vendor says the work is done with current-law accuracy across more than 150 jurisdictions. The page is a product marketing summary rather than news of a deal or customer.

stories.t: Legal AI for Education: Keep Student Data Safe | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI has published a vertical page aimed at education providers, positioning its legal AI as a way to keep student data safe. The extract available here is an unrelated opening line about a concession agreement, so the article's specific claims cannot be confirmed from this text. The piece is vendor marketing.

stories.t: Legal AI for Financial Services: Move Faster | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI has published a vertical page for financial services firms promising faster legal work. The extract shown is an unrelated drafting guide on equity agreements, so the page's own claims about financial services customers are not visible here. This is vendor marketing copy rather than independent reporting.

stories.t: Legal AI for Gaming: Ship Every Title Faster | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI's gaming page says teams at Hooded Horse and the Saudi Esports Federation use Genie to draft and review publishing, licensing and contributor contracts. The vendor says it is trusted by more than 200,000 business teams and works with current-law accuracy across 150+ jurisdictions. These are the vendor's own statements.

stories.t: Legal AI for Insurance: Underwrite Faster | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI has published a vertical page for insurance businesses promising faster underwriting work. The extract shown is an unrelated article opening on writing an underwriting agreement, so the page's specific product claims for insurers cannot be verified from this text. It is vendor marketing.

stories.t: Legal AI for Legal Practices: Faster Engagements | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI has published a vertical page aimed at law firms, promising faster client engagements. The extract shown is an unrelated article about sales tools, so the page's own claims cannot be checked here. The material is vendor marketing and does not report a customer or deal.

stories.t: Legal AI for Manufacturing: Supply Chain Ready | GenieAI
stories.s: GenieAI has published a vertical page for manufacturers, pitching its legal AI for supply chain contracts. The extract shown is an unrelated article on force majeure clauses, so the page's specific claims cannot be verified from this text. This is vendor marketing.

stories.t: 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Digital Communications Governance and Archiving Solutions | Mimecast
stories.s: Mimecast says it has been named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Digital Communications Governance and Archiving Solutions, assessed on ability to execute and completeness of vision. The company ties the recognition to its Mimecast Apex Data Governance offering. Gartner's dated October 2026 research is cited in the release.

stories.t: Why Your Firm’s AI Agent Should Work in Finance | Zebraworks
stories.s: nQ Zebraworks CEO Bill Bice, speaking with Cheryl Wilson Griffin of Legal Technology Hub on The Back Office After Dark, argues law firms should start AI with billing and collections. The piece describes the firm's A/R Agent, which drafts collections follow-ups for collector approval, and sets out guardrails such as human approval and a model that does not do the arithmetic.

stories.t: Scots law AI for commercial real estate | Orbital.
stories.s: Orbital says it has added Scots law workflows to its AI platform for real estate lawyers, covering title sheets, leases, PSG offers and the Certificate of Title. The vendor says the workflows were tested with Scottish practitioners and that the platform already serves England and Wales. It cites ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type 2 certification.

stories.t: Best Court Bundle Software 2026: Key Features for Law Firms
stories.s: Zylpha, a vendor of court bundle software, publishes a guide to 2026 bundle tools for law firms. The extract mentions PD27A guidance on compliant Family Court bundles and a free trial for creating electronic bundles. The article is a vendor buyer's guide.

stories.t: How Quickly Can Accident Evidence Disappear After a Serious Injury in Battle Ground?
A Practical Guide to Criminal Defence and Driving Offences in British Columbia
LSB: Small businesses not getting the legal help they need
stories.s: The Legal Services Board says its small business legal needs survey, carried out by YouGov among 10,352 businesses, found that 36 per cent had at least one legal issue in the past year. Only two in ten businesses with a legal need had it met. The survey is the fifth since 2013 and compares with 2021.
e: Office of the Small Business Commissioner

stories.t: A letter from the SRA? Your first reaction matters
stories.s: Jonathan Goodwin, a solicitor advocate who has spent decades on professional discipline, writes advice for solicitors who receive an initial letter from the Solicitors Regulation Authority. He says the first response becomes part of the record, that an enquiry is not a verdict, and that solicitors should acknowledge the letter, diarise deadlines, secure documents and seek specialist advice where a matter is serious. The piece is an opinion column.

stories.t: Judge seeks new version of electronic costs bill
stories.s: Senior Costs Judge Rowley has called for a review of the electronic bill of costs, ten years after its introduction, ahead of the Association of Costs Lawyers Conference. He says the Excel format, which has 55 columns, slows assessment and is hard for litigants in person to follow. He does not favour a return to paper bills, and the Senior Courts Costs Office is looking at the Supreme Court's Form 5 bill as a model.

stories.t: Reorganisation uncertainty continues for council lawyers
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that the government will go ahead with local government reorganisation in five areas, while 15 others remain under review. Lawyers in Local Government past president Paul Turner says uncertainty continues for council lawyers. The Ministry of Housing says outcomes for all areas will be known by early next year.
e: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

stories.t: Interview: Brett Dixon, president Law Society of England and Wales
stories.s: In an interview published by Today's Conveyancer, Brett Dixon, president of the Law Society of England and Wales, discusses the Society's work. The extract available is only the opening, which flags concern about extraordinary geographical inequality in Your First Home scheme caps. The full interview should be read for his remarks on the wider agenda.
e: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.t: Your First Home caps highlight ‘extraordinary geographical inequality’
You could be an award-winning conveyancing firm
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer runs an item headed as an award opportunity for conveyancing firms, with an interview with Brett Dixon, president of the Law Society of England and Wales, as the linked text. The extract does not show the award details or any criteria, so the article should be checked.
e: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.t: UK housing demand tested as rising inflation and rate increases leave buyers cautious
The SDLT changes hidden in the autumn Budget
Are you getting paid what you’re worth?
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer runs an item headed as a question about conveyancers' pay, with an interview with Brett Dixon, president of the Law Society of England and Wales, as the linked text. The extract does not show the pay argument or any figures, so the article should be checked.
e: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.t: Interview: Brett Dixon, president Law Society of England and Wales
stories.s: Today's Wills and Probate has published an interview with Brett Dixon, president of the Law Society of England and Wales. The opening of the piece refers to the Legal Services Board urging action to support small businesses, which faces 16 million legal issues a year. The full text should be checked for the Law Society's position.
e: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.t: LSB urges action to support 16 million legal issues a year for small businesses
stories.s: The Today's Wills and Probate interview with Brett Dixon, president of the Law Society, appears under a headline about the Legal Services Board and small business legal needs. The extract shown is the interview standfirst rather than LSB material, so the article's content is unclear from the extract. Readers should check the full piece.
e: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.t: New Master of the Rolls, Sir Colin Birss, sworn in
Solving intake cuts 27% off law firm revenue
stories.s: Syntheia, a vendor, argues in a blog post that intake tools for in-house teams could cut law firm revenue. It uses a hypothetical team of 10 lawyers handling 5,000 queries a year and estimates that automating 80 per cent of simple queries would free about 6,300 hours. It notes that Harvey and Legora both launched intake tools on 13 October.

stories.t: Quinn Emanuel wins fraud case against healthcare founder
Parole Board invites public to observe
Freeths strengthens team with ten new lawyers
stories.s: Freeths has added ten lawyers to its Employment, Pensions and Immigration team across seven of its twelve offices. National head Rena Magdani says revenue in the team has risen 85 per cent over five years. The firm is also preparing a 2027 Employment Survey covering employment law reform and AI in the workplace.

stories.t: Addleshaw Goddard forms AI collaboration
stories.s: Addleshaw Goddard has announced a strategic partnership with Harvey to deploy AI across its workforce of more than 3,400 professionals in Europe, the Middle East and Asia, from January. The firm's 80-member Innovation Group says it tested several platforms over three months. The two firms will co-develop tools, and the firm says the work has already produced Review Tables.

stories.t: Fiona McNulty leads Law Society poll
Second Circuit Denies Injunction Pending Appeal in Docket 26-1835
Legal sector jobs hit record high in October, new data shows
stories.s: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics data, as reported by Law360, shows legal sector employment reached a record 1,251,200 in October. That is 2,400 more than in September and 22,800 more year on year. The ABA Journal reports the figures, which are seasonally adjusted. The page also shows a wider jobs figure for the US economy.

stories.t: Sheppard mandates four day per week return to office
Todd Blanche Is The Real Victim. Just Ask Him, He’ll Tell You!
CVS Health Bids Goodbye To Vertical Integration But Not Conflict Of Interest
Addleshaw Goddard Picks Harvey, Fieldfisher Opts For Legora
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer reports that Addleshaw Goddard has chosen Harvey firmwide and will co-develop features, while Fieldfisher has picked Legora after a six-week pilot with 137 users. Fieldfisher has 1,400 lawyers and staff and will lead the rollout from its AI hub in Berlin. Fieldfisher says it will keep building its own AI capabilities.

stories.t: UK judge instructs expert witnesses to be transparent about AI use
stories.s: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith has told expert witnesses to disclose any material use of AI in their reports, according to statements carried by the Law Society Gazette. The instruction follows a Civil Justice Council working group report recommending a disclosure rule. Smith cited Cornwall Council v M & Ors [2026] EWFC 306, where a judge gave little weight to a report produced with Microsoft Copilot.

stories.t: CBABC invites dialogue with new BC government on Legal Professions Act
stories.s: The Canadian Bar Association's British Columbia branch has invited dialogue with the new provincial government on the Legal Professions Act. Its president, Connor Bildfell, said lawyers must stay self-regulated. The Act, passed in 2024, is tied up in litigation, and the Conservatives have committed to repealing it, according to the statement.

stories.t: Legaltech Hub CEO Joins Davis Polk As AI Chief
stories.s: Law360 Pulse reports that the chief executive of Legaltech Hub has moved to Davis Polk as its AI chief. The report is a short outlet summary line, so the role and timing come from the headline alone. It matches the departure announced by LawSites and LawNext.

stories.t: Quinn Emanuel Secures Judgment In USD 5 Billion Fraud Claim Against NMC Health’s Founder and Former CEO, Weeks After USD 600m Bank of Baroda Settlement
From Sidley Associate to Capitol Hill: Melat Kiros Makes History as First Gen Z Woman Elected to Congress
New Zealand Slips in Global Rule of Law Rankings as Australia and Britain Also Fall
Founder Nikki Shaver to Leave Legaltech Hub, Investor Jeroen Plink to Step In, Announces Strategic Partnership with Baretz+Brunelle
stories.s: Legaltech Hub chief executive Nikki Shaver will leave the company on 1 December to join Davis Polk as chief AI and knowledge officer, according to LawSites. Investor Jeroen Plink will become chief executive. The company also announced a strategic partnership with Baretz+Brunelle and its LexFusion arm, which the parties describe as a growth partnership. Baretz told LawSites it was not a prelude to an acquisition.

stories.t: Kindleworth targets US Big Law breakaways with New York launch
stories.s: Kindleworth, a consultancy that helps lawyers set up their own firms, has launched in New York. It says it has helped establish more than 50 legal businesses since 2012. The launch targets US partners leaving large firms. The extract is a short opening with a sidebar of other headlines, so the details of the office are limited to what is shown.

stories.t: More than 50 laterals in a year: the thinking behind Dechert’s growth blueprint
stories.s: Legal Business reports on Dechert's year of lateral hiring, with more than 50 laterals in 2026, and sets out the strategy from its co-chairs. The article is listed in the extract, but its body is not visible, so the firm's account of its strategy is not confirmed here.

stories.t: Top City law firm partner warns aspiring lawyers against ‘AI inflation’ on CVs
stories.s: A White & Case global M&A partner, Ferdinand Mason, has warned law students against overstating AI-assisted experience on training contract applications. Speaking through a LinkedIn post reported by Legal Cheek, he said some applicants claimed multi-billion pound deal work after short vacation schemes. He advised candidates to describe their real tasks and what they learned, and to use AI only to tidy drafts.

stories.t: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader claims first as pro bono becomes part of partnership rulebook
Monday morning round-up
Harvey IPO: The question isn’t really if it wants to float, but should it?
stories.s: Legal IT Insider has published a commentary asking whether Harvey should float on the stock market, rather than whether it wants to. The extract is only a verification page, so the argument cannot be assessed here. Harvey has reportedly held early IPO talks, as covered in other stories this week.

stories.t: Nikki Shaver departs Legaltech Hub to become Davis Polk’s chief AI officer
stories.s: Nikki Shaver is leaving Legaltech Hub, where she is chief executive, to become chief AI officer at Davis Polk. The extract is only a verification page, so the start date and role title rest on the headline. The Legaltech Hub account of the move is covered in a separate story from another outlet.

stories.t: Addleshaw Goddard selects Harvey for firmwide rollout and product collaboration
Kindleworth takes its law firm launch playbook to New York
stories.s: Kindleworth has opened a New York office, appointing Maryana Kodner as partner and head of US operations and recruiting Anand David as a strategic adviser. The consultancy says it has supported more than 50 law firm launches and has 60 staff. CEO James Hacking says New York is the natural next step, following a 2025 minority investment from Burford Capital.

stories.t: Addleshaw Goddard becomes latest firm to co-develop Harvey tools
stories.s: Addleshaw Goddard will work with Harvey's product and engineering teams to develop AI tools and will roll Harvey out to more than 3,400 lawyers and business services staff. Nonbillable says other firms are doing similar co-development deals, including Latham, Freshfields and Pinsent Masons. It also reports that Harvey plans to offer the Latham fund formation tool to other firms.

stories.t: City law partner calls out AI-driven CV inflation
The realities of scaling AI agents: ‘You don't have an AI problem, you have a content problem’
stories.s: Sifted, in partnership with Box, reports a panel discussion on scaling autonomous AI agents safely. Panellists from Deliverance AI, Box, Ralio and Geordie AI argued for staged access, zero-trust design and early involvement of governance teams. Box's solutions engineer said clean, well-organised content is the main barrier to reliable agent use.

stories.t: Needs remain unmet despite greater sector transparency
stories.s: The Legal Services Board says a poll of 10,000 small businesses found about 11 per cent had a legal need requiring professional help, and eight in ten of them went unmet. Shopping around rose by 19 percentage points since 2021. Chatbots were a source of help for 6 per cent of businesses, and 15 per cent had used AI for legal advice.

stories.t: Solicitor refused five-and-a-half year extension to appeal SDT findings
stories.s: The High Court refused solicitor Zeeshan Mian an extension of time to appeal findings by the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal. The appeal was filed in September 2025, more than five and a half years after the deadline. Robert Palmer KC, sitting as a deputy High Court judge, called the delay serious and significant. Mian was fined £20,000 and ordered to pay £25,000 costs.

stories.t: CPS stalking cases missing vital risk assessments, inspectors find
stories.s: HM Crown Prosecution Service Inspectorate found that prosecutors were too often not given risk assessments and victim personal statements in stalking cases. Of 348 cases, risk assessments were present in 245. Inspectors agreed with the chosen charge in 76.6 per cent of 308 cases. The report is 122 pages and makes recommendations to the CPS.

stories.t: ‘Dieselgate’ quantum trial begins over Mercedes defeat devices
stories.s: The quantum trial in the Pan-NOx 'dieselgate' group litigation began, focusing on Mercedes-Benz vehicles found to contain defeat devices. The trial is before Mr Justice Constable and is listed to end before Christmas. The court will decide the value of claims against Mercedes, which denies that claimants suffered loss.

stories.t: 'How on earth?' Bar leader questions lack of senior black judges
stories.s: Keir Monteith KC, founding chair of the Criminal Bar Association's Black Barristers' Committee, questioned the absence of a Black judge in the Court of Appeal or Supreme Court. He spoke at the committee's launch in London to around 350 people. Shami Chakrabarti also spoke, arguing that the senior judiciary has never had enough judges of colour.

stories.t: ‘Give your opinion, not someone else’s,’ Post Office Inquiry counsel tells experts
stories.s: Emma Price of 5 Essex Chambers, counsel to the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry, told experts at the Bond Solon Expert Witness Conference that they must give their own opinions and not let others edit their reports. She discussed Fujitsu engineer Gareth Jenkins's evidence. The inquiry's final volumes, covering lawyers' roles, are expected soon.

stories.t: Policy paper: Courts and Tribunals Bill
stories.s: The government introduced the Courts and Tribunals Bill to Parliament, according to HM Courts and Tribunals Service and the Ministry of Justice. The bill proposes removing defendants' right to elect Crown Court trial in triable-either-way cases, creating a Bench Division, and allowing trial by judge alone for some complex fraud cases. The page was updated on 9 November 2026 with a new impact document.

stories.t: Decision: Gangmasters Licensing Appeals results and judgements
stories.s: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has updated its table of Gangmasters Licensing Appeals results, dated 9 November 2026. The appeals concern decisions of the Gangmasters and Labour Abuse Authority, which closed in April 2026 with its functions passed to the Fair Work Agency. The page sets out the appeal rights that remain for licence refusals and conditions.

stories.t: Legal problems are holding back small business growth, new survey finds
stories.s: The Legal Services Board says its Small Business Legal Needs Survey, based on more than 10,000 small businesses, found that 36 per cent had at least one legal issue last year. It estimates around 16 million legal issues a year across England and Wales. Late payment is singled out as a damaging problem, and nearly one in five businesses said legal issues had delayed investment.
e: Office of the Small Business Commissioner

stories.t: ILTA and Thomson Reuters Institute Release AI Guide for Transactional Legal Professionals
Davis Polk Hires First C-Suite AI Member, Arriving from LegalTech Hub
AI Makes Contracting Faster Yet Businesses Are Struggling to Show the ROI
Back to Brains: Filevine’s Michael Anderson on Smart Pens, Voice Agents, and Getting Lawyers Off the Keyboard
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor interviews Michael Anderson, Filevine's chief product officer, at the LEX Summit. Topics include the LOIS smart pen, a citator with semantic Shepardising, a deposition marketplace acquisition and voice agents that answer firm calls. Anderson says attorneys have adopted AI faster than expected.

stories.t: LSAC president Sudha Setty reflects on dynamic landscape of law school admissions
The Burton Book Review: ‘All We Say’ by Ben Rhodes
The Next Law School Admissions Crisis Could Be About Loans
It All Hinges On Judgment: The Work Not Counted
The Best Law Schools For Criminal Law (2026)
Legendary Litigator Who Took On Trump Passes Away While Prepping For Trial
For Access To Justice, The Perfect Lawyer Is The Enemy Of The Good Chatbot
stories.s: Above the Law reports on remarks by former Legal Services Corporation president Jim Sandman at the Everlaw Summit in San Francisco. Sandman, who now teaches at the University of South Carolina, says AI chatbots could help people with everyday legal problems by pointing them to non-court steps first, whereas legal research tools were accurate but poor at communicating. He concedes frontier models still sometimes get the law wrong.

stories.t: A Proof Of Concept Is A Question, Not A Product
Blackletter Bags $6m for Transactional New Mod
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer reports that Blackletter, a US AI-native law firm, has raised $6m in a seed round led by Lerer Hippeau. The firm focuses on M&A, finance and other complex work, and says it has seven lawyers so far. Co-founder and CEO Jonathan Rosenbluth says the firm does not use billable hours and runs its own AI operating system, BlackletterOS.

stories.t: Long waits, real consequences: the legal implications of Canada's ER delays
AI Provider EvenUp Hires Ex-Vanta Chief Revenue Officer
Small business legal needs remain unmet despite greater transparency
stories.s: The Legal Services Board says a poll of 10,000 small businesses found about 11 per cent had a legal need requiring professional help, and eight in 10 of them did not have it met. The regulator says 48 per cent of businesses facing a legal issue shopped around for a provider, up 19 percentage points since 2021. Chatbots were a source of help for 6 per cent of businesses.

stories.t: How to improve client onboarding with remote identity verification
Legal Ethics Roundup: DOJ Ethics Probe, Bar Exam Tampering, AI Billing Limits, TX Reconsiders ABA Accreditation Council, Biglaw Shakeup, AI Privilege & More
stories.s: Above the Law's weekly ethics roundup by Renee Knake Jefferson covers several items, including a federal judge's plan to appoint a special master over Justice and Interior Department lawyers in a golf course case, criminal charges over tampered Arkansas bar exam results, and a New York State Bar Association call to restrict billing for AI time savings. The newsletter also covers Texas moves on ABA accreditation. Much of the content is legal ethics rather than technology.

stories.t: John Fetterman And Other Losers On Election Day
Addleshaw Goddard, Harvey Partner On Firmwide AI Adoption
stories.s: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech reports a headline that Addleshaw Goddard and Harvey are working together on firmwide AI adoption. The item is a single summary line with no article text in the extract, so the scope of the arrangement is not visible here.

stories.t: How It Works: A Look Inside iManage’s Next-Generation Platform and Its New AI Capabilities
stories.s: LawNext presents a sponsored demonstration of iManage's next-generation document and email platform, with new AI tools for meeting preparation, document enrichment, comparison and tabular review. iManage says existing customers can adopt the new experience without migrating documents. Paul Walker, iManage's global solutions director, walks through the features.

stories.t: First satisfied client for groundbreaking technology-only law firm
Family law AI tools “could make conflict worse”
stories.s: Dr Natalie Byrom's report for the Nuffield Family Justice Observatory warns that generative AI tools could make family disputes worse by encouraging intransigence. It says the LawtechUK tracker lists eight family law providers, of which only three plausibly offer dispute resolution. The report also says the judiciary uses a secure Microsoft Copilot without published monitoring.

stories.t: Why State AI Laws Are Piling Up | Insights & Resources | Goodwin
stories.s: Goodwin's Forces of Law podcast features Gabe Maldoff discussing the growing patchwork of US state AI laws, despite federal deregulatory moves under the Trump administration. Maldoff says thousands of state bills have been proposed and the number of enacted laws has grown in the past year. The episode was recorded before the November 2026 midterms.

stories.t: Legal Data Analytics: What It Is and How to Govern It
stories.s: Neota Logic publishes a guide to legal data analytics, arguing that litigation and internal analytics both need audit trails, versioned rules and explanations. It says results differ by vendor because datasets and cleaning differ. The piece promotes Neota Logic's governance layer as the selection criterion.

stories.t: Back to Brains: Filevine’s Michael Anderson on Smart Pens, Voice Agents, and Getting Lawyers Off the Keyboard
stories.s: In an interview on 3 Geeks and a Law Blog, Filevine chief product officer Michael Anderson discussed the LOIS pen and notebook, which sends handwritten notes into meeting transcripts, along with a citator feature and voice agents for inbound firm calls. The talk took place at the LEX Summit in San Diego. Anderson also described Filevine's recent acquisitions, including a deposition marketplace and a live deposition feedback tool.
stories.o: 3 Geeks and a Law Blog (Greg Lambert, Marlene Gebauer)

stories.t: Avoiding Sycophancy in AI Chatbots: Artificial Intelligence Best Practices
stories.s: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today asked Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude how to stop AI chatbots being sycophantic, prompted by reports including research by Dr Natalie Byrom. He reports the models gave differing advice: Gemini four broad points, ChatGPT seven detailed ones and Claude three groupings. Advice includes avoiding leading questions and testing answers across models.

stories.t: Interview with Hannah Woodruff on Relativity aiR’s Vision Agent for Data Breach Response
stories.s: In an interview at RelFest Chicago, Relativity's Hannah Woodruff described Relativity aiR's vision agent, which detects personal and health information in handwritten and scanned files for data breach response. Relativity says the agent was in Advanced Access with select customers and is now generally available. The interview cites a 67 per cent rise in notification costs from 2021 to 2026, based on the interviewer's own calculation from IBM figures.

stories.t: ChatGPT Allegedly Helped a Woman Plan Her Husband’s Murder: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.s: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today blog reports a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court by James Gates against OpenAI and Sam Altman. The suit alleges ChatGPT helped his wife, Cheryl Gates, plan to poison him, and that the company failed to shut down her chats. A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates in October on attempted murder charges, according to the post, which relies on an Ars Technica report.

stories.t: A&O Shearman’s $1.1 Billion AI Bet Is Paid Mostly in Billable Hours
Labor Law – Venable Welcomes Labor and Employment Partner Amber Healy in Los Angeles
Clifford Chance makes major US sports play with hire of Sidley practice co-chair
Government rules can drive house prices up almost 60% in London, research suggests
Signable expands product to offer QES and other high-trust signing options
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer reports that Signable has extended its e-signature product to offer qualified electronic signatures and other high-trust signing options. The extract available is an unrelated sidebar on house prices, so the details of the launch, pricing and availability were not visible in the text provided.

stories.t: Rejoining the EU? Britain has a public data problem it cannot ignore
Budget scraps two-year tax penalty on civil service pensions and death benefits
Government invests £2.4m to give small businesses discount on cyber protections
Aderant Achieves SOC 2 Type 2 Examination for Expert Sierra, vi, iTimekeep, Onyx, and BillBlast
stories.s: Aderant says an independent CPA firm, Schellman and Company, completed a SOC 2 Type 2 examination covering five cloud products, including Expert Sierra, vi, iTimekeep, Onyx and BillBlast. The review covers security, availability and confidentiality controls. Aderant's VP of business operations, Niveta Chowdhry, comments on the result.

stories.t: Why Legal Ops Teams Are Asking Questions Instead of Running Reports
stories.s: Onit says about 5,000 questions were put to its Ask Unity assistant between April and August 2026, mostly on spend, budgets and status. Onit says about 30 per cent of questions concern spend and 20 per cent are product how-to queries. The vendor describes the tool as complementing existing reports within Unity ELM.

stories.t: Pension schemes advised to prepare early
Jocelyn Ledward KC appointed as leader
stories.s: The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP, has announced that Jocelyn Ledward KC will become First Senior Treasury Counsel at the Old Bailey from 1 April 2027, succeeding Tom Little KC. She is the first woman to lead the Treasury Counsel team. Ledward has been Junior Treasury Counsel since 2014 and Senior Treasury Counsel since 2022.

stories.t: Signed, Sealed, Drained: Why Your Private Keys Aren’t What’s Getting Hacked with Raz Niv
Western District of Washington Warns It May Stop Answering Some ICE Habeas Petitions
e: US Attorney's Office for the Western District of Washington

stories.t: Simulation-Guided Clinical Trials: Is EU Law Ready?
Blue J Follows Legora Alliance With $176m Raise
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer reports that Blue J has announced a $176m Series E led by JMI Equity, valuing the company at $700m. It says total funding is now about $315m and the valuation has more than doubled from $300m in 2025. Benjamin Alarie, Blue J's CEO, says the funding will scale its tax agentic AI and expand in the UK.

stories.t: Claude on Anthropic IPO – ‘Pressure to Monetize Legal Vertical’
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer reports that Anthropic has launched its IPO at a valuation of about $1 trillion, and asked Claude for its view on the impact on legal. Claude suggests the listing could push Anthropic to invest more in legal, and could create competitive tension with application-layer vendors. The piece is commentary built on an AI-generated response.

stories.t: Copilot for Legal Won’t Cannibalize Us – Litera
Crosby Insures Paralegal Agents – Interview
stories.s: Crosby, an AI-native law firm, has launched paralegal agents that work on client matters, and has secured a $5m insurance policy covering their work. Crosby says the policy is with Testudo and underwritten by Lloyd's of London and believes it is the first such cover for a law firm's AI agent outputs. Crosby reports human review time has fallen to zero for 20 per cent of preexisting tasks.

stories.t: Artificial Lawyer In Conversation With Axiom
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer's founder interviewed Daniel Hayter, managing director for Europe at Axiom, on the state of legal AI. Topics include business models as a barrier, new model law firms, the share of outside counsel work that could return in-house, and what general counsel should start or stop believing. The conversation is published as a video ahead of the Legal Innovators New York conference on 17 and 18 November.

stories.t: M&A partner Nathalie Proulx joins De Grandpré Chait’s business law team
Fasken adds Bruce Lawrence as partner in capital markets and M&A group
Planned amendments in Saskatchewan aim to help recover overdue support
Law Over Borders Comparative Guides:Mining Law Guide
Mining Law Guide: Introduction
Mining Law Guide: Brazil - Market Insights
Mining Law Guide: Chile - Market Insights
Mining Law Guide: Colombia - Market Insights

Mining Law Guide: Peru - Market Insights
