Mining Law Guide: Venezuela - Market Insights
Tax Research Platform Blue J Raises $176M to Expand Its Agentic AI and Reach New Markets
stories.s: Blue J, a Toronto tax research and advisory platform, has raised $176m in Series E funding led by JMI Equity, according to the company. The company says the round values it at more than $700m and will fund its Workflows agentic AI and expansion into the UK and other markets. Blue J says more than 6,500 organisations use it.

stories.t: Willkie lands transatlantic Hogan Lovells Cadwalader asset management team
Addleshaws and Fieldfisher pick rival legal AI giants Harvey and Legora as adoption race heats up
stories.s: Addleshaw Goddard has agreed to roll out Harvey to more than 3,400 lawyers and staff across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, and to co-develop AI services with Harvey. Fieldfisher has chosen Legora for its 1,400 lawyers and business services staff. Legal Cheek notes Hogan Lovells Cadwalader is working with both vendors.

stories.t: ‘The competition will change’: Goodwin chair on AI and Big Law’s next era
Clifford Chance hires Sidley sports co-chair as private capital pours into sector
Chakrabarti seeks contempt exemption for jury speeches
stories.s: Baroness Chakrabarti has tabled an amendment to the Courts and Tribunals Bill that would exempt advocates who remind juries of jury equity from contempt proceedings. The move follows contempt proceedings against Garden Court Chambers' Rajiv Menon KC over a closing speech. The Lords committee begins line-by-line scrutiny of the bill today.

stories.t: Society warns of AML regulatory clash
stories.s: The Law Society warns the government must avoid overlapping regulation and extra burden as anti-money laundering reform moves through Parliament. Under the Financial Services and Markets Bill, the FCA is due to take over money laundering supervision of law firms from the SRA and other regulators at the end of 2028. Brett Dixon, the Society's president, calls for clarity on divided responsibilities.

stories.t: What Renters in California Should Ask About Building Security
Skipton Group and LMS help bring mortgage lending and estate agency closer together to improve the digital homebuying journey
Common mistakes made when buying an unoccupied property
Injunctions and their implications explained
Amidon v North London NHS Foundation Trust: EAT defines "miscarriage of justice" in whistleblowing claims
Birketts advises Bugler Group transition
Texas’ chief justice-elect wants to bring back ABA accreditation
Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years following rape and sexual assault conviction
Top Dallas County investigator arrested, charged with wife’s murder
Sheriff allows law firm to profit from policing, lawsuit alleges
stories.s: A lawsuit filed by mobile phone distributors and retailers in Miami accuses the Miami-Dade County Sheriff, Rosie Cordero-Stutz, of letting a law firm run by Israel Reyes profit from civil forfeiture cases. The companies say the firm keeps 20 to 35 per cent of proceeds, plus 5 per cent on appeal. According to October court papers, more than $45.2m was seized in cases the firm handled. The ABA Journal cites a Miami Herald story.

stories.t: Simulation-Guided Clinical Trials: Is EU Law Ready?
Legal Innovators NY – Keynote: Roberto Alarcon, White & Case
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer interviews Roberto Alarcon, Senior Manager for Innovation and AI at White & Case, ahead of his keynote at Legal Innovators New York on 17 and 18 November. He says legal innovation means practical change, that pilots need a clear problem and success criteria, and that lawyers need to frame problems and judge tool output. The piece is an interview.

stories.t: Burnout as a business risk: how workload erodes lawyers and law firms
stories.s: Canadian Lawyer reports on a panel at the Canadian Legal Summit in October, where speakers said burnout can erode law firm capacity and should be treated as a structural business risk. The panel included general counsel Carole Dagher and lawyers Jason Ward and Leanne Goldstein. The report cites the National Study on the Psychological Health Determinants of Legal Professionals in Canada, which found 59.4 per cent of legal professionals experience psychological distress.

stories.t: Ken Crutchfield: Is BigLaw Too Big To Fail? Are Other Firms Vulnerable After the Weil Wind-Down?
stories.s: Ken Crutchfield, founder of Spring Forward Consulting, writes on LawSites that Weil's wind-down exposes weaknesses in partnership models, notably low profit per equity partner and client portability rules. He says AI-native firms and managed service organisations could drive lateral moves and change how firms are financed. The piece is a guest column offering opinion.

stories.t: Latham launches $1m AI awards programme for associates
Inside FormEvo’s IHT400 Workflow – simpler, faster and calculated for you
stories.s: FormEvo, a forms provider, is promoting a live webinar on its IHT400 Workflow, a linked cloud package for HMRC Inheritance Tax accounts. The post says Inheritance Tax reforms take effect from April 2027 and that bundled forms can cut completion time by up to 80 per cent. The session is on Wednesday 18 November, 11.00am to 12.00pm.

stories.t: How we’re tackling the least digital part of conveyancing
Harbor acquires Aderant consultancy AAC Consulting
stories.s: Harbor has acquired AAC Consulting, a consultancy that works on Aderant implementations, according to the Legal IT Insider report. The extract available to us is a site verification page and does not give deal terms or the reasons behind the purchase. The deal brings a specialist Aderant services firm under Harbor's ownership, which may affect law firms that use Aderant and rely on consultancy support for it.

stories.t: Blue J announces US$176m Series E
stories.s: Blue J has announced a US$176m Series E funding round, according to a Legal IT Insider report. The extract available to us is a bot-check page, so the investors, valuation and the company's stated use of the funds are not visible here. Blue J is a tax research and AI product business, and the round adds to its capital for product development.

stories.t: Sullivan & Cromwell steps in to secure futures of eight Weil trainees
Mistral pushes back on new AI copyright proposals, sparking outcry from creatives
stories.s: French creative workers, including writers, journalists, musicians and artists, have criticised Mistral, the French AI model maker, after it pushed back on a new law proposal on the use of copyrighted material in generative AI. The extract is a short article opening and does not name the proposal's sponsors or the specific changes Mistral opposes.

stories.t: How we’re tackling the least digital part of conveyancing.
stories.s: InfoTrack's head of product, Louise Edwardes, writes in Today's Conveyancer about how its conveyancing products link together to help with pre-completion work. The item is the same piece as a Legal Futures article carried the same day. It cites the Digital Conveyancing Maturity Index 2026 and says 81 per cent of firms still review pre-completion risk manually.

stories.t: Form: Order a transcript of court or tribunal proceedings: Form EX107
stories.s: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has updated form EX107, used to order a written transcript of a court or tribunal hearing. The page notes that from 10 November 2026 it updated the addresses for Acolad in the English and Welsh guides. It also lists earlier changes, including transcription costs for civil, family and tribunal hearings updated in June 2026.

stories.t: Harbor Acquires Aderant-Focused Consultancy AAC
Weil's Head of AI Looks to Rehome Halted Summer Associate Tech Program
Tax Law Platform Blue J Raises $176M Series E Round
Lindsay Clancy loses bid to dismiss murder case with retrial possibility
A Press Secretary Comeback? Katie Zacharia May Be Ready For Her Close-Up
Biglaw Begins Hiring Trump Collaborators As They Flee DOJ
Goodwin Associates Can Take Home Up To $140K In Bonuses, Plus A Raise In 2027
Trump’s DOJ Ran Off So Many Lawyers It Can’t Even Show Up To Keep People Locked Up Anymore
stories.s: Above the Law reports that the US Department of Justice under the Trump administration has lost so many lawyers that it can no longer always send staff to court to keep people in detention. The extract is a short teaser and does not give figures, the cases affected or the department's response. The story is dated 10 November 2026.

stories.t: The Top Law Schools For Tax Law (2026)
LSA bencher candidates talk Regulated Professions Neutrality Act at town hall
stories.s: Law Society of Alberta bencher candidates discussed the Regulated Professions Neutrality Act at a town hall. The law bans regulators requiring EDI or cultural competency training, and the society has dropped its EDI committee in response.

stories.t: AI-Powered Firm Raises $6M In Seed Funding Through MSO
Legal Tech Co. Harbor Global Acquires AAC Consulting
stories.s: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech reports that Harbor Global, a legal technology company, has acquired AAC Consulting. The outlet's summary line is the only text available, so the reported terms, price and rationale for the deal are not known from this item. The story is dated 10 November 2026.

stories.t: Former GE, EY Leaders Join Wood Smith MSO Board
2 Attys Fined For AI Citation Errors But Local Counsel Spared
stories.s: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech reports that two attorneys have been fined over citation errors in filings that involved AI tools, while local counsel was not sanctioned. The outlet's summary line is the only text available, so the court, the amount of any fine and the reasoning are not visible here. The story is dated 10 November 2026.

stories.t: AI Law Firm Crosby Inks $5M Malpractice Insurance Policy
stories.s: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech reports that Crosby, which it describes as an AI law firm, has bought a $5m malpractice insurance policy. The outlet's summary line is the only text available, so the insurer, premium and policy terms are not visible here. The story is dated 10 November 2026.

stories.t: Weil partners approve wind-down plan in firmwide vote
Weil partners approve wind-down after weeks of turmoil
Judge Gonzalez Rogers dismisses with leave to amend Google’s First Amended Complaint for DMCA anti-circumvention claims v. SerpApi
stories.s: Edward Lee's blog tracks AI copyright litigation and notes that Judge Gonzalez Rogers has dismissed, with leave to amend, Google's First Amended Complaint on DMCA anti-circumvention claims against SerpApi. The judge had earlier dismissed the original complaint on similar grounds. The claims concern Google's SearchGuard system and scraping of Google results.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Cooley Adds Top AI and Technology Transactions Partner in San Francisco // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley has hired Barath Chari as a partner in its San Francisco technology transactions practice, from Wilson Sonsini Goodrich and Rosati. Cooley says he advises on AI, software and IP transactions. The firm says the group has more than 40 lawyers and that the firm has nearly 1,400 lawyers across 19 offices. TJ Graham, chair of the group, welcomed the hire.

stories.t: Key Themes In State Bank Supervisors' AI Exam Framework // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley lawyers Kate Goodman, Jasmine Banks and Mari Dugas wrote a Law360 article on the Conference of State Bank Supervisors' new AI supervisory framework for state-chartered banks and nonbank lenders. They highlight governance, third-party oversight, data privacy and consumer protection. The page also lists earlier press mentions of Cooley. The authors are Cooley lawyers writing in their own voice.

stories.t: FCC Advances US Cyber Trust Mark Program, Labeling and Certification Requirements // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley reports that the FCC released a Public Notice on 27 October 2026 seeking comment on the US Cyber Trust Mark for consumer IoT products. Proposals include a QR code, three-year certification renewal and 90-day evaluation by Cybersecurity Label Administrators. Chairman Brendan Carr named Commissioner Olivia Trusty to lead rollout. The rules are not yet final.

stories.t: Ninth Circuit Leaves SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 Reporting in Place, Blocks Scope 3 and SB 261 // Cooley // Global Law Firm
stories.s: Cooley reports that the Ninth Circuit has left SB 253 Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas reporting in place, while holding SB 253 Scope 3 and SB 261 likely unconstitutional under the First Amendment and warranting preliminary relief. The decision was issued on 9 November 2026. The firm says California may seek rehearing or Supreme Court review, and the district court must consider severability.

stories.t: A MoFo Privacy Minute Q&A: When AI Agents Attack, How Can Traditional Incident Response Processes and Legal Frameworks Keep Up? | Morrison Foerster
stories.s: Morrison Foerster's Privacy Minute series considers how incident response and legal frameworks can cope with AI-enabled attacks that spread across corporate networks quickly. The firm says existing breach notification duties still apply.

stories.t: AI in construction: the good - the current landscape of AI in construction
stories.s: Trowers & Hamlins publishes the first of a construction AI series, describing where AI is already used in design, planning, cost, site safety and contract work. The firm argues that governance and accountability must keep pace with deployment. The piece sets out opportunities and legal risks for the construction sector.

stories.t: AI in construction: the bad and the ethical
stories.s: Trowers & Hamlins publishes the second part of its construction AI series, setting out eight risks including incorrect outputs, biased data, cybersecurity and unclear liability. The firm recommends pilots with governance, AI literacy and explicit human accountability. The series is aimed at construction leaders and their advisers.

stories.t: Four brands face ban due to misleading ad claims
Law Society warns against double regulation
stories.s: The Law Society of England and Wales has warned that the Financial Services and Markets Bill's anti-money laundering reforms could create overlapping regulation for law firms. Ahead of second reading on 10 November, it asks for clarity on the split between the Financial Conduct Authority and legal sector rules. President Brett Dixon says the reforms must not result in over-regulation.
e: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.t: Irwell Insurance sees record growth milestone
AI should not replace experts’ views
stories.s: Mrs Justice Joanna Smith, speaking at the Bond Solon Expert Witness Conference in London, said AI cannot replace expert opinion and responsibility stays with the expert. She introduced a Civil Justice Council working group report on responsible AI use in court documents. The Bond Solon and Law Society Gazette Expert Witness Survey 2026 found 45 per cent of experts use AI for reports, and 70 per cent want disclosure of AI's role.

stories.t: Youngest magistrate in South Yorkshire
Law Firms Are Reshaping Teams for AI, but Few Are Managing the Cost of Delivery
stories.s: BigHand says its Law Firm Talent and Resourcing Report 2026, based on a survey of more than 800 law firm leaders in the UK and North America, finds 99 per cent say AI is changing hiring and team mix. Only 22 per cent consider matter profitability when allocating work. The vendor also cites DLA Piper, a BigHand customer, saying it saved over 600 hours and £673,000 in resourcing time by the half-year point.

stories.t: Salesforce CPQ End-of-Sale: What it Means for Your Contracts
stories.s: Docusign publishes a piece on how its contracting tools connect with Salesforce CPQ, which Salesforce is ending sale of. The extract is only the opening line, so the specific end-of-sale details are not shown here.

stories.t: Managing the First 30 Days After a Data Breach | Relativity Blog | Relativity
stories.s: Array and Relativity held a webinar on the first 30 days after a data breach, with experts from Norton Rose Fulbright. Relativity's Hannah Woodruff said that in typical breach matters only around 5 to 20 per cent of data may need review. The post stresses early scoping and triage, and early intelligence from Relativity aiR. Relativity published the piece on its own blog.

stories.t: Prudent AI: Accelerate Reversible Learning, Pace Irreversible Commitment
Western Washington U.S. Attorney Signals It Can’t Oppose Every Immigration Habeas Petition
e: US Attorney's Office, Western District of Washington

stories.t: Professionalism Spotlight on Yulanda Curtis: ‘A Veteran’s Legal Problem Rarely Exists in Isolation’
Claude Code is Accidentally Exposing Your Info on GitHub: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.s: Doug Austin, citing an Ars Technica report, says Apiiro researchers found Claude Code settings files with secrets in public GitHub repositories. About 1,100 files from 63 organisations contained secrets, out of over 100,000 uploaded settings files. The leak relates to stored command approvals. Anthropic's Boris Cherny said the team is looking at prevention.

stories.t: Five Reasons to Standardize Your ESI Protocol: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.s: Doug Austin, writing on eDiscovery Today, summarises a Nextpoint resource giving five reasons to standardise an ESI protocol. The list covers planning, data protection, identifying difficult data sources, reuse for third-party data and a reference for the matter. Nextpoint offers a 13-question checklist. The post is sponsored by Nextpoint, which is named as an Educational Partner.

stories.t: Orchestrated Workflows Govern Coordination of eDiscovery: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.s: Doug Austin relays an Exterro article by Bryant Bell arguing that eDiscovery technology does not manage coordination, and that orchestrated workflows do. The piece says coordination tasks such as custodian confirmation and hold tracking happen between systems. Exterro is named as an Educational Partner and sponsor of the blog. The original article is linked.

stories.t: Digital Fortress: Protecting the deal - Cybersecurity and data protection in real estate
stories.s: Mishcon de Reya's Digital Fortress series discusses cyber threats to the real estate sector, including payment diversion fraud, business email compromise, ransomware and data breaches. The firm says these incidents can disrupt transactions and damage reputation. The extract is a summary line, so the practical guidance is not visible.

stories.t: Why We Call The Old-Line Firms ‘White Shoe’
Zhihe AI Launches Agent 3.5 and 70 Open Legal AI Skills
e: Shanghai Intelligeast Network Technology Co., Ltd.

stories.t: Scott Bomhof boosts restructuring and insolvency offering at Davies
Elvis Presley Enterprises claims Suno violated Tennessee’s ELVIS Act
Adjudicator relied on ‘phantom’ citation to remove refugee status: Fed. Court
stories.s: The Federal Court of Canada, in Horvath v. Canada, sent a refugee status decision back to the Immigration and Refugee Board after finding it relied on a nonexistent Federal Court quotation. Judge Angus Grant ruled on 3 November; the lawyer says AI was not raised in the proceedings.
e: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada

stories.t: Atty Can't Duck Sanctions Over Alleged AI Fake Citations
Franchise Law – New Book Tackles New Zealand’s $73 Billion Franchising Industry and Its Legal Gaps
Senior judges back review of electronic bill of costs
Businessman fails in claim against opponent’s solicitors
stories.s: Mr Justice Eardley struck out a claim by Raj Pal Senna against Lewis Silkin, which concerned trade mark proceedings for Hoya Corporation. The judge said the claim was bound to fail and certified it as totally without merit. He held that the immunity from suit for statements made in legal proceedings was a complete answer. Senna sought at least £375,000 in damages.

stories.t: Judge attacks dishonest claimant’s “scandalous” behaviour
stories.s: Mr Justice Mansfield found that Vengadeswara Raw Gopalakrishnan fundamentally dishonest over a claim worth about £7m, stripping him of costs protection. The Home Office relied on surveillance video showing him at the gym and in a go-karting competition. The judge ordered him to pay costs up to discontinuance. The claim had been run through a litigation friend, and the judge described it as having been dishonest since 2014.

stories.t: Regulator calls for 2,000 more conveyancing lawyers
e: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

stories.t: Why good governance matters when managing Law Society forms
stories.s: FormEvo, a Law Society licensed forms provider, argues in a sponsored post that firms need structured governance of Law Society forms. It cites the 6th edition of the TA6 property information form, released in March 2026, as an example. The post says local copies and manual checks create compliance risk. FormEvo says it works with the Law Society to deliver official forms.

stories.t: Who could replace Palantir in the NHS?
stories.s: Sifted reports that the UK government is reportedly preparing to extend Palantir's NHS contract, reported at £330m, by two years. The move would give time to find an alternative to the American data analytics company. The extract cites reporting rather than an official notice.

stories.t: Why Europe’s AI founders are opening accounting and law firms
stories.s: Sifted reports that dealmaking is accelerating for AI-native professional services firms in Europe, with investors backing start-ups that aim to challenge slower incumbents. The extract is a single summary line, so the article's named firms, deals and figures are not visible here. The piece covers accounting and law firms opened by AI founders.

stories.t: Judge praises 'progressive policing' to protect vulnerable woman
stories.s: Mr Justice Hayden, sitting as the out of hours judge, granted Devon and Cornwall Police an urgent order in Re X to stop a young woman leaving the country and to add passport and travel restrictions. He found that she would likely have been killed if she had returned. He praised the police investigation as progressive policing of the highest calibre. No findings have been made on her allegations.

stories.t: Stalking victim dismayed by ‘useless’ SRA response to reports
stories.s: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has been criticised after a blogger, Daniel Cloake, says he forwarded dozens of emails from solicitor Andrew Milne to the regulator in 2024 without a substantive response. Milne lost his appeal against a stalking conviction at Snaresbrook Crown Court. The judge said his role was not to assess the SRA's handling. The SRA says it cannot comment on matters under disciplinary proceedings.

stories.t: Law Society warns of AML ‘double regulation’ ahead of oversight transfer to FCA
stories.s: The Law Society has asked the government to avoid double regulation of the legal profession when anti-money laundering oversight moves to the Financial Conduct Authority. President Brett Dixon says the Law Society supports efforts to tackle economic crime. The extract is a single summary line.

stories.t: LSB urges action to support 16 million legal issues a year for small businesses
stories.s: The Legal Services Board says a survey of more than 10,000 businesses shows legal problems hold back investment and growth. Four in 10 legal matters cost more than £5,000 and one in ten cost more than £15,000. The LSB urges action to support small businesses with around 16 million legal issues a year. The extract is a single summary line.

stories.t: Trainee solicitor and paralegal handed section 43 orders by SRA over child sexual abuse convictions
stories.s: The SRA has issued section 43 orders against a paralegal and a trainee solicitor following child sexual offence convictions. The orders restrict where and how Toby Everden can work in a regulated firm. The extract is a single summary line, so the second individual and the dates are not visible here.

stories.t: Law Society warns of AML ‘double regulation’ ahead of oversight transfer to FCA
stories.s: Today's Wills and Probate carries the same Law Society warning on AML double regulation ahead of the FCA oversight transfer. The extract shows only a related line about a consumer panel backing the Legal Services Board shake-up. The Law Society says it backs efforts to tackle economic crime but wants to avoid duplicate regulation.

stories.t: Trainee solicitor and paralegal handed section 43 orders by SRA over child sexual abuse convictions
stories.s: Today's Wills and Probate reports that the SRA has handed section 43 orders to a paralegal and a trainee solicitor after child sexual offence convictions. The orders restrict their work in regulated firms. The extract is mismatched and shows a Law Society AML item, so the names and details need checking in the full article.

stories.t: Continuous Improvement: The Secret to Sustainable Firm Growth
stories.s: Actionstep, a practice management vendor, publishes a piece on continuous improvement, describing Maison Chen Law Group, a Melbourne migration firm that grew from four to thirty lawyers. The vendor says the firm's admin time per matter fell from 2.5 hours to just over half an hour and that it appointed a Continuous Improvement Officer.

stories.t: Dye & Durham to Host First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Conference Call
stories.s: Dye & Durham, the Toronto-listed practice management software provider, will release its first quarter fiscal 2027 results on 12 November 2026, followed by a conference call hosted by its interim CEO and interim CFO.

stories.t: Elevate Experts Steve Harmon and Mike Fry on the Future of AI-Powered Entity Management
stories.s: Elevate says its general counsel and chief operating officer, Steve Harmon, and entity management vice president, Mike Fry, wrote an Association of Corporate Counsel article on AI in entity management. The piece is a November 2026 vendor publication.

stories.t: Announcing the 2026 Everlaw Summit Award Winners
stories.s: Everlaw has announced the winners of its 2026 Summit Awards, now in their fifth year, honouring customers and partners. Winners include Reed Willis of Align Technology, who moved litigation review to AI-assisted review, and Greg McCullough of Fire Litigation Consulting. The awards include three new partner categories for managed service providers.

stories.t: Your GRC Platform Is Only Half the Answer. Who’s Helping You Run It?
stories.s: Mitratech promotes its GRC practitioners, using a Jan Stappers profile to argue that buyers need people who have done the work as well as AI features. The piece is a vendor marketing post for its governance, risk and compliance offering. The extract is a summary line, so specifics about services are not visible.

stories.t: How Should In-House Legal Teams Prepare for Rising Consumer Protection Litigation?
stories.s: Onit argues in-house teams should test intake, legal hold, outside counsel and spend processes against rising consumer protection litigation. It cites Lex Machina's report of 20,353 federal filings in 2025, up 31 per cent.

stories.t: Three Things Legal Ops Won’t Stop Talking About This Year
The 5 inputs behind better investigations
stories.s: Thomson Reuters CaseLines published a short infographic setting out five inputs that help investigators surface risk and speed due diligence. It promotes Thomson Reuters CLEAR Investigate as the tool for reducing data overload.

stories.t: How legal expertise is built into CoCounsel Legal
stories.s: Thomson Reuters says CoCounsel Legal is built on attorney-editors from Practical Law and Westlaw, more than 1,300 of whom shape its content, reasoning and benchmarks. The article presents this as its Fiduciary-Grade AI approach.

stories.t: Washington Judge Keeps Zillow Antitrust Suit Alive Over Mortgage Steering Claims
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports that a federal judge in Washington has denied Zillow's request to reconsider an earlier ruling, so the proposed antitrust class action Dupuis v. Zillow can continue on its mortgage steering claims. The suit alleges Zillow pressured affiliated agents to steer buyers to its mortgage products. The ruling does not decide the merits.

stories.t: AI Connectors For E-Discovery: Great To Drive, But There Are Speed Limits
Harvey Forum Chicago: GCs Talk About Increasing Expectations Due to AI
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reports on a Harvey Forum in Chicago where general counsel discussed rising expectations of AI. Robert Rivkin, chief legal officer at United Airlines, said companies will likely try to do as much as possible with AI before assigning matters to outside counsel. The extract is a single quote, so the wider discussion is not visible.

stories.t: NCSC scheme will help critical organisations test their cyber defences
stories.s: The National Cyber Security Centre has launched its Cyber Adversary Simulation (CyAS) scheme, an assurance scheme for suppliers of adversary simulation testing. The NCSC says providers will be assessed against an NCSC-defined standard and will build customer-specific attack plans. The scheme starts as a minimum viable product, letting the NCSC test demand before a fuller operating model. It sits alongside the Cyber Assessment Framework and the Cyber Resilience Audit scheme.

stories.t: Morning Docket: 11.11.26
stories.s: Above the Law's Morning Docket for 11 November 2026 rounds up US legal news. Items include an ethics charge against Alina Habba over an NDA dispute, a judge removing a DOJ attorney from a case, and a Texas incoming chief justice proposing to restore an ABA accreditation requirement. The newsletter also covers SEC enforcement figures and a defamation suit against the BBC.

stories.t: Legora Targets Public Sector With Ex-Minister
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer reports that Legora is expanding Lucy Frazer KC's role, from adviser since July to leading its public sector work, and says she will be part-time and based in London. Legora says courts and government legal teams need AI they can trust. The company cites the Crown Court backlog of 80,829 cases at the end of June 2026.

stories.t: Mercedes Lawyer Joins AI Native Compound Law
Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing call off merger
‘We now ask the AI first’ – exclusive new research reveals how AI is transforming in-house legal
Nvidia brings in Wachtell for investigation into CEO’s alleged affair with Chinese spy
Sullivan & Cromwell rescues current and future trainees as Weil partners approve wind-down
Keystone’s AI funds tool – “We’re solving a problem using tech in the right way”
stories.s: Legal IT Insider has published an interview headlined around Keystone's AI funds tool, in which the company says it is solving a problem using technology in the right way. The extract available here is only a site verification notice, so the substance of the interview cannot be confirmed from it.

stories.t: Former Cabinet minister Lucy Frazer KC to lead public sector drive by Legora
stories.s: Legal IT Insider reports that Lucy Frazer KC is to lead Legora's public sector work, according to the headline. The extract available is a site verification notice, so the detail of her role cannot be checked from it. Artificial Lawyer separately reports that Frazer, a former Cabinet minister, will lead public sector partnerships.

stories.t: GenieAI “spins up entire team of agents for each workflow”
stories.s: Legal IT Insider has published a piece on GenieAI, quoting the company's claim that it spins up an entire team of agents for each workflow. The extract available is a site verification notice, so the detail of the product cannot be confirmed from it. GenieAI has published a large run of product pages in the same period.

stories.t: How Lisa’s Law migrated 14 years of data to LEAP Enterprise
stories.s: Legal Practice Management reports that Lisa's Law, a London firm of around 75 people, moved from a case management system it had used since 2012 to LEAP Enterprise. The firm migrated 73 users and 14 years of matter data, with Thinkwild also involved. The article is presented as a vendor-supported case study from LEAP.

stories.t: Latham puts $1m behind its associates’ best AI ideas
Willkie adds Hogan Lovells Cadwalader PE head in five-partner transatlantic raid
Weil partners vote to formally wind down Wall Street firm
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that Weil Gotshal and Manges partners voted 97 per cent in favour of an orderly wind-down, handing the process to a committee. About 1,200 lawyers and more than 1,000 staff are affected. The Gazette says Sidley Austin is in talks to hire around 200 from Weil and that Kirkland & Ellis will take 40 Weil lawyers.

stories.t: Lords clash over 'Stalin' clause in courts bill
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that peers clashed over a clause in the Courts and Tribunals Bill that would let ministers add offences to the non-jury list without full parliamentary scrutiny. Lord Keen of Elie criticised the 'Henry VIII powers' and withdrew his amendment, with the issue to return at report stage. Lord Lemos said the power would let the system respond to evolving fraud, including developments in AI.

stories.t: Industry panel event highlights property law’s biggest threat: AI competition, part one
stories.s: Today's Conveyancer carries a summary of a Search Acumen panel at the Digital Conveyancing Summit in October. The panel addressed AI competition as a threat to property law, according to the outlet, and this is part one of a series. The extract is only an outline, so the panel's conclusions are not visible here.

stories.t: Claren launches Envoys to take on in-house legal work
stories.s: Claren has launched Envoys, which it describes as AI employees for in-house legal teams. According to the outline, Envoys picks up requests from Slack, Teams and email and escalates risky items. The extract is a single summary line, so further product detail is not available here.

stories.t: HIGHCOURT launches offline agentic AI system for law firms
Piepenbrock v LSE: EAT rules on bankruptcy and standing to pursue employment appeals
ABA President Barbara Howard says association will continue to prioritize the defense of democracy
Weil Gotshal partners vote to dissolve firm
stories.s: Weil, Gotshal & Manges partners have voted to dissolve the nearly century-old firm, with 97 per cent approving according to Law.com. A three-person committee will oversee the wind-down, with restructuring officers from AlixPartners and Davis Polk. Law.com also reports that the restructuring chair Matt Barr and several bankruptcy lawyers are in talks to join Skadden, and that the firm lost nearly 50 partners in 2026.

stories.t: What happened at Weil Gotshal? Could tech help other firms avoid that fate?
stories.s: ABA Journal's Legal Rebels podcast interviews Noah Waisberg, CEO of Zuva and a former Weil Gotshal associate, about the firm's wind-down and whether technology could help other firms avoid a similar fate. Waisberg previously led Kira Systems, which was sold to Litera in 2021. The episode is by Victor Li.

stories.t: The ACLU Doesn’t Do Impeachment, But It Had Some Thoughts About Pete Hegseth
Is Cahill Gordon The Next Weil? Partner Exits And Acquisition Talk Have Biglaw Guessing
Chuck Grassley Says Democrats Are Stonewalling Judges ‘For The First Time In Our Nation’s History.’ Merrick Garland Would Like A Word.
Claren Launches ‘Envoys’ Inhouse Agents
Legora Taps Ex-Solicitor General To Boost Public Sector Deals
stories.s: Law360 Pulse reports that Legora has hired a former Solicitor General to build its public sector business. The extract is only the outlet summary line, so the individual's name, start date and remit are not available here. The item is a people move at an AI legal technology vendor.

stories.t: ‘It can get really ugly’ – Weil braces for litigation as wind-down begins
stories.s: Legal Business reports that Weil, Gotshal & Manges is braced for litigation as its wind-down begins. Albert Togut of Togut Segal & Segal is quoted saying that all those involved in law firm failure are lawyers, so any of them can start litigation without outside counsel. The extract also lists related Weil coverage, including a partner vote on the wind-down plan.

stories.t: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing call off merger talks
Latham unveils $1 million bonus pot to reward lawyers driving AI innovation
stories.s: Latham & Watkins has launched a $1 million awards programme, the Associate AI Impact Award, to reward associates who build AI tools or improve workflows. The firm has set aside the sum for 2027 and says all associates across its global offices may take part. Michael Rubin, chair of the firm's AI practice, says the award aims to scale useful ideas. Winners have not yet been named.

stories.t: New judicial review guidance explained – AI use & urgent applications
stories.s: Brabners, writing for Legal Futures, explains new Administrative Court guidance. The Judicial Review Guide 2026 adds a section on AI tools, warning court users to take reasonable care when citing authorities, and sets page limits. A separate Practice Statement tightens urgent applications, with urgency judged solely on Form N463. Brabners says the guidance is essential reading for parties to judicial review.

stories.t: BigHand Report finds law firms restructuring for AI without managing the cost of delivery
stories.s: BigHand's Law Firm Talent and Resourcing Report 2026, based on a survey of more than 800 law firm leaders in the UK and North America, finds that AI is changing hiring for nearly all firms but few track matter profitability. Clients are pressing on AI-related pricing, according to 46 per cent of firms. BigHand says 16 per cent combine structured processes, technology and budgets. DLA Piper is cited as a customer.

stories.t: Practice-area searches to law firms fell 36% this summer as name searches held steady, research finds
stories.s: MLT Digital's report Search Has Moved. Has Your Firm? uses Google data from 99 law firm websites in Scotland, England and Wales, and Ireland. It finds that clicks for practice-area searches fell 35.8 per cent between June and August 2026, against the same months of 2025, while firm-name searches held steady. MLT links the drop partly to Google AI Overviews, and the agency is offering a free review.

stories.t: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing call off merger talks
Hogan Lovells Cadwalader adds HSF Kramer DCM head in London
Stephenson Harwood - Taylor Wessing merger called off
stories.s: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing say they will not proceed with a planned merger, which had been under discussion and was due for a partner vote by the end of 2026 ahead of a possible May 2027 combination. The joint statement cites initial discussions and mutual agreement. Taylor Wessing became independent in June after its UK arm merged with Winston & Strawn.

stories.t: Solicitor appeals strike-off over Munich remote-hearing lie
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that Priyank Tanwar, struck off in January 2026, is appealing the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal's finding that he misled Leicester County Court about his location during an August 2023 hearing. His counsel argues the tribunal over-relied on the transcript. The SRA opposed the appeal, which was heard before Thomas Raphael KC, sitting as a deputy High Court judge.

stories.t: Form: Apply for a court order to make arrangements for a child or resolve a dispute about their upbringing: Form C100
stories.s: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has updated Form C100, the application for a child arrangements, prohibited steps or specific issue order under the Children Act 1989. The form can be filed online or on paper, and a mediation information meeting is required before most applications. The page history records an 11 November 2026 update to the Welsh form.

stories.t: Form: Apply for an inherent jurisdiction order in relation to children: Form C66
Form: Apply to internationally transfer a court application involving children to or from England and Wales: Form C68
Guidance: Gender Recognition Certificate: list of medical practitioners in gender dysphoria
Guidance: Expert adviser on the future of criminal courts for children
Why Blue California Voters Rejected Implementing The Nation’s First Wealth Tax
No Just Moving On: We Demand Vengeance Against MAGA, And Getting It Will Help Lower Costs
Congressional Democrats Are Ready To Turn Up The Heat On Biglaw’s Trump Deals
D&L: Daeryook & Aju and Lin Merge in South Korea
stories.s: Daeryook & Aju and Lin signed a merger agreement in Seoul on 9 November 2026 to form D&L. The combined firm will have 397 Korean-licensed lawyers and combined 2025 revenue of 143.7 billion won, and the firms expect registration in mid-December 2026 or later. Daeryook & Aju will be the surviving entity, and the firms describe the deal as a merger of equals.

stories.t: Vote for the top insurance defence specialized firms 2027-28
BigLaw Breakaways Fuel Kindleworth’s New York Expansion as Partners Seek Independence
Does Your Budget Tell You No, or Tell You Where to Go?
Court wants to know if Keker law firm is still representing Perplexity AI
stories.s: Commentator Edward Lee reports that Judge Engelmayer has asked whether Keker Van Nest still represents Perplexity AI or intends to withdraw. The question follows Perplexity's late withdrawal of its motion to have Proskauer act for it, after Proskauer raised a potential conflict from its earlier work for the opposing party. The post sits within a tracker of AI copyright and tort litigation.
stories.o: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.t: Less is More: SEC’s Division of Enforcement Year-End Results Reflect Shift Toward More Targeted Enforcement Amid Decline in Actions and Monetary Remedies
stories.s: The Debevoise & Plimpton client note reports that the SEC's Division of Enforcement announced fiscal 2026 results on 10 November 2026, the first full year under Chairman Paul Atkins and the first annual results under Director David Woodcock. The headline points to a shift to more targeted enforcement and fewer actions. The extract is only a summary line.

stories.t: OCC’s New “Super Intelligence” Supervisory Framework: Key Takeaways and How It Compares to the FSB’s AI Sound Practices
stories.s: Debevoise & Plimpton reviews the OCC's Supervisory Framework for Bank Use of Super Intelligence and compares it with the FSB's AI sound practices. The firm says the framework signals how US bank regulators may approach AI supervision.
e: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

stories.t: Digital Fairness Act: the EU’s new consumer protection rulebook takes shape | Freshfields
stories.s: Freshfields analyses the European Commission's Digital Fairness Act proposal, published on 11 November 2026. The proposal would replace the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive with a directly applicable Regulation covering dark patterns, influencer marketing, subscriptions and addictive design. It would also let the Commission investigate directly and impose fines.

stories.t: Ninth Circuit Leaves Core California Emissions Disclosures in Place | Morrison Foerster
stories.s: The Ninth Circuit declined to block SB 253's Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions disclosures but held Scope 3 and SB 261 likely breach the First Amendment, according to Morrison Foerster. The opinion is not a final merits ruling.

stories.t: CFTC Declares DCMs’ Use of Geographic Access Restrictions Inconsistent With Impartial Access Requirements | Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP
stories.s: Skadden says the CFTC has approved guidance on 5 November 2026 that designated contract markets generally may not restrict access based on a trader's location within the US. DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions within 30 days or explain why they cannot comply. The guidance responds to state court orders against prediction markets offering sports event contracts.

stories.t: Oman data privacy tool
stories.s: Trowers & Hamlins has published a free online Data Privacy maturity assessment tool for businesses preparing for Oman's PDPL. Users receive a maturity assessment, commentary and recommended next steps across awareness, governance, consent, data subject rights and security. The extract is a short product notice and gives no publication date.

stories.t: CFTC Addresses Domestic Geographic Restrictions on DCM Access
stories.s: Willkie Farr & Gallagher has published a note on a CFTC position addressing domestic geographic restrictions on designated contract market access. The extract is only an outlet summary line, so the detail of the CFTC position is not visible here. The note concerns derivatives market access rather than legal technology.

stories.t: Ninth Circuit Finds Certain Aspects of California’s Climate Risk Disclosure Laws Likely Unconstitutional, While Preserving Core Emissions Reporting Requirements
stories.s: Willkie Farr & Gallagher reports that the Ninth Circuit found some aspects of California's climate risk disclosure laws likely unconstitutional, while keeping core emissions reporting requirements in place.

stories.t: Bevan Brittan expands with new partner
Ministry of Justice cuts impact court support
stories.s: Support Through Court, a national charity helping people in civil and family courts, says a £300,000 funding cut from the Ministry of Justice has closed its services in Chelmsford and Southend. The charity says it assisted on 51,116 occasions last year and is appealing for the decision to be reversed. Its chief executive Emma Taylor and former Supreme Court President Lord Neuberger both voiced concern.

stories.t: Kindleworth expands operations with New York office
stories.s: Kindleworth, a London-based consultancy that helps lawyers launch their own firms, has opened a New York office. Maryana Kodner joins as Partner and Head of US Operations, and Anand David as Strategic Advisor. The firm says it has supported over 50 law firm launches globally.

stories.t: Protect the Value You Negotiate with Ironclad + Ramp | Ironclad
stories.s: Ironclad promotes a December webinar with Ramp on linking procurement, legal and finance in one contract workflow. The vendor says about 11 per cent of contract value leaks after signature. The session will demonstrate purchase requests triggering Ironclad contract workflows and synced obligations.

stories.t: What Is a Gap Assessment? A Guide for Legal Teams
stories.s: Neota Logic publishes a guide explaining gap assessments for legal departments and law firms. It distinguishes gap assessment from risk assessment and describes compliance gaps as unmet, partly met or undocumented requirements. The article argues that governed AI use is the most urgent current gap and that visibility of AI tools is usually the first step.

stories.t: AI Accuracy, Capability, and Reliability: What's the Difference? | Relativity Blog | Relativity
stories.s: Relativity says legal teams should separate the terms accurate, capable and reliable when evaluating AI tools. Accuracy concerns a single correct output, capability means a tool can do a task, and reliability means consistent performance at scale. Aurora Bryant, senior manager of applied legal intelligence at Relativity, is quoted on the distinctions.

stories.t: How AI Thought It Earned Its Rigor Badge (and Failed the Test)
SEC’s FY 2026 Enforcement Results Show Fewer Cases, Sharper Priority Signals
stories.s: Legal Tech Monitor reviews the SEC's fiscal 2026 enforcement results, announced on 10 November, which show fewer actions but a focus on investor protection, public-company reporting and trading integrity. The article notes an action involving Archer-Daniels-Midland and suggests in-house counsel should not relax controls.

stories.t: How Should Legal Teams Evaluate Legal Hold Software?: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.s: Shelley Bougnague of Cloudficient argues that legal hold software should be judged as a preservation system, not just a tool for notices and acknowledgments. She recommends testing products against realistic matter scenarios. The post promotes Cloudficient's CaseFusion product, which covers identification, legal hold and targeted collection, and is published on eDiscovery Today with a disclosure that Cloudficient is a sponsor.

stories.t: Getting the Workflow Right and Preparing for What’s Coming with AI: Artificial Intelligence Best Practices
stories.s: Discernis, a sponsor of eDiscovery Today, argues that in-house counsel should treat AI as an investigative intelligence tool rather than an automation tool in corporate investigations. The final part of its series covers workflow structure, regulatory context and preparation. The post stresses that AI handles high-volume review well but cannot exercise legal judgment.

stories.t: MPs call for legislation to overturn Carter-Ruck privilege ruling
stories.s: MPs are urging the government to legislate so that the September High Court ruling in Carter-Ruck does not stop regulators reaching privileged material. Labour MP Phil Brickell, speaking on the second reading of the Financial Services and Markets Bill, warned of a risk that wrongdoing by solicitors would go unscrutinised. The bill would move AML supervision of lawyers and accountants to the FCA, with the transition due to begin in 2028.

stories.t: Former judge sets out how to do “the best job in the world”
stories.s: Sir Peter Coulson, retiring from the Court of Appeal, has published a book, The Practice of Judging, and spoke to Legal Futures about judicial life. He discusses rising workloads, the three-month judgment expectation and the growing number of litigants in person. He says he is sympathetic to their use of AI, describing it as often the only friend they have.

stories.t: Law firms taking out more and bigger loans to fund growth
stories.s: Barclays research of 125 senior leaders finds that 93 per cent of law firms are likely to increase investment over the next year. Loan balances among legal practices rose 12.7 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 on the year, and 32 per cent of firms say they have redesigned their business model to use AI fully. Skilled labour shortages affect 63 per cent of firms' growth.

stories.t: From chat to Cowork: preparing your law firm for agentic AI
stories.s: Matthew Stringer, founder and CEO of Legal Futures, writes that law firms should weigh agentic AI before moving further into it. He separates conversational AI from agents that plan steps and act across connected systems, and describes standing mandates that let an agent act on defined events. He proposes five tests for any use: repeatable, checkable, supervised, bounded and worth it. Stridon, his consultancy, estimates an agent briefing could cost around £2-5.

Solicitor fined £10,500 over AML and account breaches
Half of homebuyers would pull out of purchase if the home had a flood risk
Government invests £2.4m to give small businesses discount on cyber protections
Trustees being forced out of mainstream banking, STEP warns
Solicitor fined £10,500 over AML and account breaches
stories.s: This page carries the same headline as the SDT fine story, but its extract is an unrelated item about trustees being forced out of mainstream banking, according to STEP. The extract does not confirm the fine itself, so the underlying story should be checked against the original report.

stories.t: Compliance with Celeste: Trust, not just technology
stories.s: Intapp describes Celeste, its Firm AI product, as an operating layer for professional firms, and explains how firms can keep control. Celeste uses the requesting user's credentials, admins choose the model for each job, and a person reviews requests before submission. The post sets out chat, assistant and coworker layers and promotes the product.

stories.t: The Third Partner: Why Shepherd & Co. Trusts Dye & Durham for Cashiering
stories.s: Dye & Durham, in a vendor feature in Quill, describes how Shepherd & Co. outsources cashiering to a dedicated Dye & Durham cashier. The piece says reconciliations were brought up to date within about a fortnight after the partners took over, and that the arrangement has run for seven years.

stories.t: Lawyers’ Day 2026 in Georgia: International Conference on “Lawyers and the Effective Protection of Rights: Challenges in the Era of Artificial Intelligence” – CCBE
stories.s: CCBE has published a notice about Lawyers' Day 2026 in Georgia, an international conference on lawyers and the effective protection of rights in the age of artificial intelligence. The extract is brief and reads as a conference announcement, with a heading on the International Criminal Court. Details of speakers, dates and format are not visible in the extract.

stories.t: Intellek launches AI Readiness training for legal teams
Shepherd and Wedderburn expands with family law
SRA 2026/27 Business Plan published
stories.s: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has published its final 2026/27 Business Plan, setting out three priorities: operational excellence, proactive risk identification and focusing on the biggest issues. It reports a 45 per cent rise in misconduct reports between 2022 and 2025 and plans a proactive supervision function. Chief executive Sarah Rapson says the plan marks the next stage of the reset.

Democrats’ Midterm Wins Could Reshape Healthcare Access For Underserved Americans
Is Big Law ‘AI Gaslighting’ Us?
stories.s: Artificial Lawyer's opinion piece asks whether large law firms' high-profile AI investments and announcements benefit clients or are mainly marketing. The author suggests firms share measurable client benefits, such as lower fees on AI-assisted matters and faster delivery. The piece is commentary and does not report a new deal or product.

stories.t: Keeping Legal AI Connected: Why Your Data and Case Should Work Together
stories.s: Marla Crawford, general counsel at Cimplifi, argues in a guest column that legal teams adding many AI tools risk scattering data and work product across disconnected systems. She says this creates problems for defensibility, control and cost in litigation and eDiscovery. The column promotes Relativity aiR as the system of record where work should come together.

IP Law News – Quarles Adds AI and Data Governance Partner Megan Bowman to Minneapolis Office
Gibson Dunn confirms Weil co-managing partner among 120-strong transatlantic funds lift
stories.s: Legal Business reports that Gibson Dunn has confirmed it has hired a 120-lawyer private funds team from Weil, including 23 partners and Weil co-managing partner Jonathon Soler. The group joins offices in New York, Washington DC and London. The move follows Weil's decision to wind down.

stories.t: Freshfields and Goodwin match Milbank scale for US associates
SQE set to generate £59 million in fees as SRA seeks to rebuild confidence in exams
stories.s: Legal Cheek reports that the SRA's 2026/27 business plan forecasts £59.1m in education and training income from SQE candidate fees, and £60.9m in spending. The SRA will cut SQE1 questions from 360 to 340 from January 2027. The latest SQE1 overall pass rate was 42 per cent in July, down from 53 per cent in January.

stories.t: Dentons posts 90% retention score for trainees and apprentices
The personal injury justice gap: Why injuries are rising but claims are falling in 2026
stories.s: National Claims argues that personal injury claims have fallen sharply, citing ACSO figures of 413,323 claims registered in 2025 against more than 876,000 in 2018, a fall of 53 per cent. It cites HSE data on about 680,000 non-fatal workplace injuries in 2024/25 and suggests people may be deterred from claiming.

stories.t: Perfect Portal launches new payments service with lower handling charges and greater flexibility
stories.s: Perfect Portal has launched One Percent Payments, a payment service built with InfoTrack and powered by Mollie. It charges a 1 per cent handling fee on standard domestic credit and debit card payments, with other methods possibly higher. The service is available to firms using both Perfect Portal and InfoTrack.

stories.t: SRA to explore “alternative regulatory tools” to investigations
stories.s: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has published its final business plan for the year to 31 October 2027. It plans to explore alternatives to formal investigations, such as supervisory dialogue or conditions on authorisations. The plan raises the practising certificate fee share by £50 to £240 to raise an extra £25m, with £23m for IT and change programmes. Misconduct reports rose 45 per cent to 16,499.

stories.t: TalkingTech Podcast: New Outlook risks and the rise of open source in legal
Simpson Thacher joins Kirkland and Paul Weiss in ending financial disclosures
Legora taps former minister for government push as legal AI moves well beyond law firms
stories.s: Legora has appointed former Cabinet minister Lucy Frazer KC to lead its global public sector partnerships, starting with the UK and Europe. Frazer has advised the Swedish company since July. Nonbillable reports that Harvey, Clio and LexisNexis are also courting government customers, and that a Thomson Reuters survey found over a quarter of government legal professionals now use AI.

stories.t: Ex-Clifford Chance lawyer bets on AI agents for in-house legal work
stories.s: Claren, founded by former Clifford Chance lawyer Gus Neate, has launched Envoys, AI agents that take in-house legal requests, apply playbooks and escalate to lawyers. Neate says the US is now the fastest-growing market and the company raised $1.7m in pre-seed funding last year. Claren, formerly Wilson AI, says it is not currently seeking new funding.

stories.t: Law firms have a new way to measure how good their lawyers are at AI
stories.s: Harvey commissioned a five-level AI fluency framework for lawyers, developed by legal AI consultant Peter Duffy of TITANS. It uses platform usage data rather than self-assessment. CMS Netherlands says it took part in the research, and NautaDutilh has referenced the framework in a recruitment advert.

stories.t: Charity forced to close court support services after MoJ funding cut
stories.s: Support Through Court, a charity helping people who face civil and family courts without a lawyer, is closing its Chelmsford and Southend services after a £300,000 annual cut in Ministry of Justice funding. Its chief executive, Emma Taylor, says further reductions may become unavoidable without alternative funding. The charity is urging the government to reconsider and has asked supporters to contact MPs and ministers.

stories.t: 29% fee rise will bring about 'real change', SRA pledges
stories.s: The Law Society Gazette reports that the SRA's 2026/27 business plan lifts the practising certificate fee to £240 from £190 and raises income from practising fees by 29 per cent to £111.5m. Compensation fund contributions rise from £26m to £46.3m. Law Society president Brett Dixon says the extra cost should be short term and called for independent LSB assessment.

stories.t: Collapsed firm's staff find new home as 400 files acquired
stories.s: Ridley & Hall, a Yorkshire firm, is opening a Harrogate office after acquiring 400 family and property cases from Berwins Solicitors, which appointed administrators the previous week. It has recruited six former Berwins staff, including Michelle Crowhurst and Danielle Day. Managing director Emma Pearmaine says the firm aims for £7m turnover in its centenary year.

stories.t: New proposals to stop childhood crimes closing doors for life
stories.s: The Ministry of Justice has launched a consultation on ending lifelong disclosure for some childhood convictions, removing disclosure of out-of-court resolutions and reducing disclosure of fines. Serious violent and sexual offences would be excluded. Minister Jake Richards says the plans give young people a fair chance, and the consultation launches ahead of Alan Milburn's review.
